A status btrfs cannot report answers 500, not idle (test_a_status_that_btrfs_cannot_report_is_an_error_not_idle), and the card then says 'Could not read the scrub status' instead of a stale progress and still offers Cancel Scrub (spec 'a scrub status that cannot be read says why instead of a stale progress'); a start or cancel that btrfs did is answered running or aborted when the status read after it fails (test_a_start_or_cancel_whose_status_cannot_be_read). Step 4: test_scheduler_validation.py test_scrub_task, test_scrub_of_an_unmounted_pool_fails_without_btrfs, test_a_scheduled_scrub_is_recorded_when_btrfs_returns. Step 5: storage.spec.ts 'shows pool health and mount state' and the unmount spec (no Scrub on a pool that is not mounted). The 409 of the API for an unmounted pool is storage.scrub-needs-mounted-pool. Open, on the device, on the pool data: Scrub on the Storage page shows the progress moving and a result at the end ('Last scrub: No errors' on a healthy pool), Cancel Scrub on a second run shows 'Last scrub: cancelled before it finished', a scheduled scrub task's Run now is recorded as success, the API answers other requests meanwhile, and the SD writes of the run are measured (the scrub status lives in the /var/lib/btrfs tmpfs, ADR-0171); and the re-check after the owner's reboot (ADR-0018), after which the pool shows no last scrub result: the restart forgot it (ADR-0171). Device check 2026-11-08 after the deploy of main 1fdf802: a scrub of the pool data ran to the end in 19 s with 0 errors and its progress moving; a second scrub was cancelled (aborted). Right after the start, GET .../scrub still says idle for a moment. The re-check of 2026-11-09 (PROGRESS.md, Log) found step 2 failing on the device: for about 6 s after Start Scrub the API answered idle, Start Scrub's own answer too, until btrfs had recorded the new scrub, so the page stopped following a scrub that ran and offered Scrub again. Fixed by ADR-0313, which superseded ADR-0272: a scrub is running when btrfs prints its time left, also below "no stats available", and Start Scrub answers running when the status read right after it says idle (TestScrubStatus: the status of a scrub btrfs has not recorded yet, test_start_answers_running_before_btrfs_reports_the_scrub; 5.9 s of idle measured after a start); the copy of a disk replace, which the kernel runs as a scrub, is not shown as one when no record shows it (test_the_copy_of_a_disk_replace_is_no_scrub), and a cancel that btrfs did answers aborted when the status then says idle (test_a_cancel_before_btrfs_recorded_the_scrub_answers_aborted). Device check 2026-11-09 with main eceead5, ADR-0313 deployed: scripts/dev/scenario.sh scrub passed at 21:11 UTC and, after the reboot of 21:12 UTC (the boot of 21:14:01 UTC), at 21:17 UTC: Start Scrub answered running and so did the status right after it; the scrub of data ran 18 s, its bytes scrubbed growing from 0.42 to 1.28 GiB (1.27 after the reboot), and finished without errors; a second scrub, cancelled once btrfs had recorded it, ended aborted; a disabled scheduled scrub task's Run now said "Scrub started", and its scrub finished after 19 s, while one of a folder with nothing mounted on it failed with "Pool <name> is not mounted at <path>" (0.152 and 0.148 MiB; that no btrfs runs then is test_scheduler_validation.py test_scrub_of_an_unmounted_pool_fails_without_btrfs); the first step found the pool's last scrub idle both times (the smbconf check before it restarts the supervisor, ADR-0171); the whole check 0.555 and 0.543 MiB. The Storage page itself was not looked at on the device: its card is the E2E specs' on route fakes (ADR-0215), and the device check covers the API that the card reads. Since ADR-0314 the device check is scripts/dev/scenario.sh scrub: the start's answer, a scrub to its end with its bytes scrubbed growing, a cancel and a scheduled scrub's Run now, with each step's SD MiB; its first step names the pool's last scrub, which a reboot leaves none of (ADR-0171).

features.description: An administrator reads the SMART data of every disk the Storage page lists and schedules SMART tests
steps: On Storage or System > Disk Health, open a disk: its SMART attributes, temperature and overall health are shown
Disk Health lists the same disks as Storage, NVMe included, and disks without SMART data too
A partition or another device is refused as not a disk of this system
In System > Scheduler, a SMART test task offers the connected whole disks and keeps the disk of a task while it is disconnected
Run now records the run as success, failed or timed out
features.notes: Disk Health opens each disk's SMART data in a dialog, from what GET /health/disks returned (ADR-0235): health, temperature, power-on hours and cycles, serial, firmware, the last self-test (of the ATA or the NVMe self-test log), the ATA attributes with their status, and the SMART/Health Information log of NVMe disks (test_health_smart.py, health.spec.ts on route fakes). smartctl runs in the container (architecture.host-command-layer), and GET /health/disks runs it without -n standby, so opening Disk Health wakes sleeping disks (storage.disk-spindown). Device check: 2026-11-06 (slice 1 deploy: SMART data and a short test of the pool's disk). Open: the device check of the dialog (System > Disk Health on the device: the pool's disk /dev/sda opens with its attributes, temperature and PASSED; an NVMe disk, if one is connected, with its health log) and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018). Device check 2026-11-07 after the deploy of main cce0def: GET /api/v1/health/disks returned the SMART data of /dev/sda (WDC WD6400AACS: health PASSED, 33 C, 51832 power-on hours, 17 attributes, the last short self-test), and again after a reboot.

features.description: SMART attributes are recorded over time, and a rising count of reallocated or pending sectors raises an alert
steps: The SMART monitor records each disk's attributes at every pass
A rise in reallocated or pending sectors sends an alert to the e-mail and Telegram channels
GET /api/v1/health/smart/trends and /smart/predictions report the trend and a failure estimate per disk
features.notes: Proven here, 2026-11-07. Step 1: test_health_monitor.py TestSmartHistoryWrites test_every_pass_is_recorded_in_ram_where_the_endpoints_read_it (each pass adds the disk's counters, temperature and path, as /smart/history, /smart-monitor/status and /smart/trends report), test_health_smart.py test_the_monitor_checks_the_same_disks (every awake whole disk of Disk Health) and test_storage.py test_monitor_round_runs_in_a_worker_thread. The history is written only when a pass changes it and at shutdown (ADR-0269, ADR-0214): TestSmartHistoryWrites proves that passes that change nothing and a start that changes nothing write nothing, that a new disk, a counter, a path or an lsblk serial writes it at once, that a failed write is tried again and the alert still sent, and that the snapshots in RAM are written at shutdown. Step 2: TestSmartAlertChannels (a rise of the reallocated or of the pending sectors reaches every enabled e-mail and Telegram channel once, not a disabled one, with the title, message and recommendation) and TestSmartTrendAlerts (one alert per rise, again for a further rise, none after a snapshot without the counters, again for a rise after a drop, ADR-0270); TestSmartHistoryWrites test_a_pass_that_ends_after_the_shutdown_keeps_nothing_and_alerts_at_the_next_start (ADR-0269; an alert still being sent when the supervisor stops is cut off, as before); test_storage.py TestAlertsOffTheEventLoop (delivery off the event loop, bounded). Step 3: TestSmartTrendsEndpoint (GET /api/v1/health/smart/trends lists every tracked disk with its data points and rising counters, steady and removed disks included, the disks without a serial or with an empty one by path, the window of the last 24 values, ADR-0270) and test_smart_predictions.py (GET /smart/predictions: the failure estimate of each connected disk, ADR-0235). Only the ATA counters are recorded, so NVMe disks have none, and sleeping disks are skipped (smartctl -n standby). No host-level change. A sanity check after the next deploy: GET /api/v1/health/smart/trends lists the device's disks with data_points growing by one per hour, and /data/smart_history.json keeps its mtime across hourly passes (stat), so the hourly SD writes of the old monitor are gone (scripts/dev/sd.sh measure over a pass). Reviewed in a fresh context twice (ADR-0017), 2026-11-07 and 2026-11-08; the findings were fixed except two, recorded in ADR-0269 and ADR-0270: an alert still being sent when the supervisor stops is cut off and not sent again (the monitor writes before it sends, as before), and a history that an older monitor stored under an empty serial is not continued under 'unknown'.

features.description: Disks whose SMART trend predicts a failure are marked replace soon on the dashboard and in Disk Health
steps: A disk with a predicted failure shows replace soon with the reason
The mark goes away when the prediction does
features.notes: GET /health/smart/predictions scores the SMART history as ADR-0235 fixes it (the rate over the last 24 snapshots; no prediction for NVMe disks or the shared 'unknown' history) and covers the disks connected now, found by the lsblk serial the monitor stores with each snapshot when it names one disk and one history, else by path. A counter is read from the snapshots that hold it, and the history file is written atomically; one that cannot be read answers 500. Disk Health marks a disk Replace soon by its serial, with the risk factors and the recommendation, and lists a prediction that matches no listed disk apart; the dashboard lists such disks for administrators and links to Disk Health; both say when the predictions cannot be read. Proven here, 2026-11-07: test_smart_predictions.py (the threshold, the window, snapshots without the counters, the disks covered, the mark going a day after the last rise, the history file), health.spec.ts and dashboard.spec.ts on route fakes, roles.spec.ts (no request for regular users); reviewed in a fresh context twice (ADR-0017), the findings of the second fixed on 2026-11-07. No host-level change, and no failing disk can be shown on the device. A sanity check there after the next deploy: GET /api/v1/health/smart/predictions answers 200 for the connected disks, new snapshots in /data/smart_history.json hold lsblk_serial, and the dashboard shows no mark and no warning.

features.description: The Snapshots page lists the copies that snapshot restores made, and deletes them
steps: Restore a snapshot of a volume: the copy restore_<time> is listed on the Snapshots page
Delete it there after the check that nothing uses it: the subvolume is removed by its subvolume id
The volume that held it can be deleted afterwards
features.notes: Until 2026-11-12 a restored copy inside a volume could be deleted nowhere in the web UI. Built 2026-11-12 (ADR-0358): GET /snapshots/copies?subvolume=<pool or volume> lists the copies that restores made right in a pool or a volume (a writable snapshot restore_<date>_<time>, its path checked byte for byte, Parent UUID set and not read-only), newest first with the time of the name, and DELETE /snapshots/copies/{name}?subvolume=... deletes one by btrfs subvolume delete --subvolid after the checks of a volume's Delete (running containers, SMB shares, NFS exports, the off-device copy; one function for both now, pools._refuse_used_subvolume), refusing anything else (400, 404, 409); the audit log gets snapshot_deleted. features.description: A btrfs or smartctl command that hangs in the kernel no longer holds a worker thread after its timeout
steps: A scrub, stats reset or SMART test command that does not return is killed at its timeout, and its worker thread is free at once
The API answers the timeout, and later requests are served
features.notes: Built (ADR-0290, which superseded ADR-0289 after the review): btrfs scrub start, status and cancel (the Storage page and scheduled scrubs), btrfs device stats --reset, smartctl -t (POST /api/v1/health/disk/{device}/test and scheduled SMART tests), the reads of SMART data (Disk Health, the Storage page's SMART data and the hourly SMART monitor) and the btrfs subvolume show of the scheduler's snapshot cleanup (which had no timeout and now has 60 seconds) run through host.run_in_container. It starts the command in a session of its own; at the timeout it kills the command's process group with SIGKILL, leaves the wait for its end to a daemon thread and raises TimeoutExpired at once. It runs one run of a command at a time: a second run waits for the first and starts once it ended, and while a killed run is still stuck the command is not started but fails at once, logged once as "Not started", so a hung pool or disk keeps at most one stuck process of each command. A SMART test without an answer now says "smartctl did not answer within 30 seconds: <device> may not be responding" instead of "Command timed out"; a snapshot cleanup whose btrfs does not answer deletes nothing, and the snapshot task's run fails with "Snapshot <name> created, but old snapshots were not cleaned up: btrfs did not answer within 60 seconds. The pool may not be responding.". Step 1: tests/test_command_timeouts.py: TestRealProcesses (a timeout ends the command and the sleep it started, as nsenter starts its command, and no other process; a session of its own) and TestCommandsThatDoNotReturn (with fake processes whose wait never returns: the timeout raised at once, the process group killed, the wait left to a daemon thread, a stuck command not started again, a second run that waits for the first until it is killed and then starts nothing, a second run that starts as soon as the first answered); TestScrubStart of test_storage.py and test_a_scheduled_scrub_is_recorded_when_btrfs_returns of test_scheduler_validation.py run fake btrfs scripts through the real runner. Step 2: tests/test_command_timeouts.py through the API with one worker thread of each kind: POST, GET and DELETE /api/v1/storage/pools/<pool>/scrub, POST /api/v1/health/raid/<pool>/reset-stats, POST /api/v1/health/disk/<disk>/test, GET /api/v1/storage/disks/<disk>/smart, GET /api/v1/health/disk/<disk> and GET /api/v1/health/disks answer the timeout, then serve the next request at once, and answer at once while the command is stuck; a scheduled scrub and SMART test fail with their message and free the scheduler's thread, a scheduled snapshot task whose cleanup gets no answer fails and keeps the snapshots, and the SMART monitor records the other disks; test_a_stats_reset_that_does_not_return_answers_500 of test_health_monitor.py; test_a_snapshot_task_whose_cleanup_btrfs_does_not_answer_is_recorded_as_failed of test_scheduler_validation.py (the run and the task's last status are failed). Because scrubs and SMART reach the host's pools and disks (a host-level change), the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018), with the SD MiB of each step (ADR-0214), were needed. On the dev device: POST /api/v1/storage/pools/<pool>/scrub answers 200 within seconds, GET /api/v1/storage/pools/<pool>/scrub then says running and `ps -o pid,sid,pgid,args` shows the scrub's btrfs process with its own session, and DELETE /api/v1/storage/pools/<pool>/scrub cancels it; POST /api/v1/health/raid/<pool>/reset-stats answers 200; POST /api/v1/health/disk/<disk>/test?test_type=short answers started; GET /api/v1/health/disks, GET /api/v1/health/disk/<disk> and GET /api/v1/storage/disks/<disk>/smart answer with the disk's data; Run now of a BTRFS Scrub, a SMART Test and a BTRFS Snapshot task with a keep count records success; `docker logs unos-supervisor` has neither a "Killed" nor a "Not started" warning; and after a reboot the same. A process stuck in the kernel cannot be made on the device on purpose: that part is shown by the fakes only. Not covered: the Snapshots page's commands (run_cmd of src/snapshots/router.py, also the scheduled snapshot itself) still use subprocess.run, since they name their folders by descriptor numbers and their list would have to stop at the first btrfs that does not answer; the Storage page's scrub status polling does not wait for each answer, so on a hung pool its overlapping requests hold the default executor's threads for one timeout (docs/USER_GUIDE.md says so), after which the card says 'Could not read the scrub status' with the timeout (ADR-0272); the commands of host.run_on_host still run on, on the host, after their timeout, which frees the thread (architecture.host-command-layer). Device check 2026-11-11 (tree 8ea5a08, by hand, before and after the reboot from the API at 23:22:13 UTC on 2026-11-11 (the boot of 23:23:10; both containers healthy by 23:23:59)), the same both times: POST /storage/pools/data/scrub answered running in 0.5 s, ps showed 'btrfs scrub start /mnt/pools/data' alone in a session of its own (its sid and pgid its own, not the supervisor's), and DELETE cancelled it (aborted after 5 to 6 s); reset-stats answered ok; GET /health/disks, /health/disk/sda and /storage/disks/sda/smart answered with sda's data (WD-WCAUF0349104, PASSED); POST /health/disk/sda/test?test_type=short started a self-test that completed without error; Run now of disabled Scrub, Snapshot (keep count 1000) and SMART Test tasks recorded success ('Scrub started', 'Snapshot auto_<time> created', 'SMART test started') and their scrub and self-test ended without errors; the task snapshot was deleted again; docker logs of unos-supervisor held neither Killed nor Not started. SD MiB of the whole check 0.480 before and 0.591 after the reboot. A command stuck in the kernel cannot be made on the device on purpose: that part rests on the fakes, as above.

features.description: Storage operations stay correct with rare names, races and Docker states
steps: A subvolume renamed while the quota rollback guard runs is never taken for the new volume
Odd subvolume names, line breaks included, cannot confuse what UNOS reads from btrfs subvolume list
When Docker cannot be asked during an unmount, a Docker volume's mount of the pool is not taken for the administrator's own mount
Docker volumes are compared with bind folders after resolving symlinks and relative paths, also for third-party volume drivers
Whole disks named like xvdaa, sdaaa or dasda are accepted wherever they are listed
A failing subvolume list right after a volume create answers that the volume exists without its quota, and a create whose name was taken meanwhile names what is there
Renaming or moving a folder that is a bind mount answers 409, not 500
A folder delete stops at a mount or subvolume that appears below the folder while it is deleted
features.notes: Low-severity cases deferred in slice 1; each step can be a pass of its own. 2026-11-11: steps 3 and 7 fixed and tested with fakes; steps 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 8 were open then (see 2026-11-12 below). Step 3 (ADR-0344, which supersedes ADR-0070): when Docker cannot be asked about the running containers or their volumes, Unmount and Remove Pool of a mounted pool answer 503 "Pool '<name>' was left mounted: Docker did not answer, ..." before anything changes (no umount, no fstab write, no unmount in a mount namespace); a pool that is not mounted is still removed without Docker. test_pool_persistence.py: test_without_docker_the_pool_stays_mounted_and_nothing_changes (a Docker volume's host mount of the pool, for unmount and remove), test_docker_volume_that_cannot_be_inspected_leaves_the_pool_mounted, test_without_docker_a_container_that_binds_the_pools_mountpoint_is_refused and TestPoolEndpoints test_unmount_and_remove_without_docker_answer_503_and_change_nothing failed before (the pool was reported unmounted, or unmounted and mounted again); they replace the tests of ADR-0070's unmount without Docker. Step 7: a rename, or a move within the pool, that rename(2) refuses with EBUSY (a folder that is a bind mount of another folder of its pool, whose st_dev is the pool's) answers 409 with the text of a delete of it, "'<name>' is a separate subvolume or filesystem (such as a snapshot or a mount point) and cannot be renamed (moved) in the file manager."; any other EBUSY of the file API answers 409 "In use by the system, for example as a mount point, so the file manager cannot change it" (it answered 500). test_files_security.py: test_a_folder_that_is_a_bind_mount_cannot_be_renamed_or_moved (EBUSY faked, the mount in the fake mount table) and test_any_other_entry_that_is_busy_is_a_conflict failed before (500 "File operation failed: <the text of EBUSY>"). Open for steps 3 and 7: the device check. A Docker that does not answer while the supervisor runs cannot be made safely on the device (a stopped Docker stops UNOS), so step 3 rests on the fakes. Step 7 on the device: on a test pool, bind-mount one folder onto another with mount --bind (on the owner's request), then Rename and Move of that folder in the File Browser answer 409 with that text and change nothing; unmount the bind mount afterwards. Report the SD MiB of each step. ADR-0348 (which supersedes ADR-0170): a move checks every item in the mount table before any is moved, so a bind mount among several items moves none of them (test_a_move_refuses_a_bind_mount_before_anything_is_moved failed before: the first item had moved), and a move that fails part way says how many items moved before it (test_a_move_that_fails_part_way_says_how_many_items_went_before failed before). A file that is a bind mount is looked up in the mount table whatever its st_dev, also before a move to another pool (test_a_move_refuses_a_file_that_is_a_bind_mount_with_another_st_dev failed before: the first item had moved, and to another pool the file had been copied and the answer was "In use by the system"). Not checked on the dev device yet: step 7 with a real bind mount (mount --bind on a test pool); step 3 cannot be made on the device safely. 2026-11-12: steps 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 8 fixed and tested with fakes (ADR-0352, which supersedes ADR-0073). Step 1: the quota guard of a new volume takes as the newest id before the create the higher of the first line of `btrfs subvolume list --sort=-rootid` and the first level-0 line of `btrfs qgroup show --sort=-qgroupid`; a subvolume keeps its quota group 0/<id> while a rename takes it out of the list. test_volumes.py TestQuotaRollback test_a_subvolume_renamed_while_the_guard_reads_is_never_taken_for_the_new_volume failed before: with the swap after the create the renamed subvolume got the quota (200), with the swap when the quota failed it was deleted ("The volume was removed again."). Step 2: with the highest id first, a line that a name with a line break adds cannot raise the newest id; and every id the list gives a volume name is checked by the host's shell, which compares `btrfs inspect-internal subvolid-resolve <id>` with the name byte for byte (_VOLUME_PATHS_SCRIPT), for the list, a delete and the quota. test_a_name_that_forges_a_higher_id_costs_later_volumes_nothing failed before (409 "it was renamed or replaced right after it was created ... existed before it was created"), TestDelete test_a_name_that_starts_with_a_volume_name_and_a_line_break_is_another_subvolume failed before (the delete went to the id of "photos\nold", 257, not to 256) and test_such_a_name_alone_is_no_volume too ("photos" was listed). Two tests changed with it: test_forged_list_line_cannot_swap_volumes and test_a_forged_list_line_does_not_move_the_quota (renamed from test_a_forged_list_line_gets_no_quota) expected 409 and now expect the real volume deleted or limited, the forged id untouched; test_forged_list_line_cannot_redirect_the_delete no longer lists the phantom. Step 4: for an unmount, Remove Pool, Delete Volume and an import under an earlier pool's name, each Source of a container's mounts and each folder a local volume binds is made absolute (from /), resolved by `realpath --canonicalize-missing` on the host and located in the host's mount table (MAJ:MIN and FSROOT): it counts when it lies in the folder of the pool or volume (_containers_on). test_volumes.py TestVolumeInUse test_a_container_that_reaches_the_volume_another_way_keeps_it (symbolic link, relative link, relative device, device through a link, folder bound on the host, third-party driver) failed before (200, the volume deleted), and test_pool_persistence.py test_refuses_a_container_that_reaches_the_pool_through_a_link_or_another_mount (symbolic link, folder bound on the host; unmount and remove) failed before (DID NOT RAISE PoolBusyError: the pool was unmounted). Step 5: DISK_NAME_PATTERN also takes sdaaa, xvdaa, dasda, dasdaa and their partitions; lsblk still decides what is a disk. test_health_smart.py test_whole_disks_with_longer_names_answer_wherever_they_are_listed (GET /storage/disks/<name>/smart, GET and POST /health/disk/<name>), test_disk_safety.py test_creates_a_pool_on_a_disk_with_a_longer_name and test_scheduler_validation.py test_disks_with_longer_names_are_targets failed before with 400 "Invalid disk name format. Expected format like 'sda', 'sdb1', or 'nvme0n1'" (pool create: "Invalid device name format"). Step 6: a list or check that fails right after a create with a quota answers 500 "Volume '<name>' was created without its quota: ... Delete it and create it again.", and a create that btrfs refuses because something took the name meanwhile answers 409 "'<name>' already exists in pool '<pool>': <a folder|a file|a symbolic link|a subvolume> took the name while the volume was being created. Nothing was created." (stat --format='%i %F' on the host). TestCreateRaces test_a_failing_list_after_the_create_says_that_the_volume_exists_without_its_quota (500 "Listing the subvolumes of /mnt/pools/data failed: ...") and test_a_name_taken_after_the_check_is_a_conflict_that_names_what_is_there (500 "Creating volume 'documents' failed: ERROR: target path already exists: ...") failed before. Step 8: a delete for good of a folder (also Empty trash, the expiry and a move to another pool or volume) walks it on descriptors and checks each folder's st_dev and mount ID (/proc/self/fdinfo) before deleting anything in it (_remove_tree): a subvolume or mount that appears below the folder after the checks stops it with 409, which says that part of the folder was deleted before that. test_files_security.py test_a_delete_stops_at_a_subvolume_or_mount_that_appears_below_the_folder_while_it_runs (a subvolume, a bind mount) failed before: 200, the folder was deleted with the files of the new mount. Open: the device check, with the SD MiB of each step (ADR-0214): on a test pool with quotas enabled, a volume created with a quota gets it (the real btrfs-progs with --sort=-rootid, --sort=-qgroupid and subvolid-resolve in the script); a subvolume made by hand with the name of a volume, a line break and more is not listed and does not stop the delete of that volume; a container that binds a symbolic link to a volume keeps Delete Volume from deleting it; SMART data of a disk only if one with a long name is attached. A mount that appears during a delete cannot be timed by hand: the fakes carry step 8. Accepted (ADR-0352): a stale quota group above every subvolume can make a create with a quota answer 409 after its id is given out again following a remount, and FUSE or network volume drivers are not recognized. Review fixes 2026-11-12 (ADR-0352): realpath runs under the host's timeout --signal=KILL 10; one that does not answer answers 500 before anything changes ("Pool '<name>' was left mounted: realpath did not resolve ...", "Volume '<name>' was not deleted: ..."); a list or check that does not answer after a create with a quota answers 500 "Volume '<name>' was created without its quota: btrfs did not answer within 120 seconds. Delete it and create it again." and keeps the volume. test_a_realpath_that_does_not_answer_leaves_the_pool_mounted, test_a_realpath_that_does_not_answer_keeps_the_volume and test_btrfs_that_does_not_answer_after_the_create_says_that_the_volume_exists_without_its_quota failed before. 2026-11-12: a realpath killed by timeout's SIGKILL reaches the supervisor as -9 (nsenter re-raises it); -9 now counts as a hang, as 124 and 137 do (the -9 cases failed before: 'exit status -9'). A btrfs qgroup limit that does not answer answers 500 "Volume '<name>' was created, but btrfs did not answer within 120 seconds while its quota was set: it may have no quota. Delete it and create it again." and keeps the volume (test_a_quota_limit_that_does_not_answer_says_that_the_volume_may_have_no_quota failed before). Device check 2026-11-12 (main 641f2a5, before and after the reboot from the API at 04:35:30 UTC on 2026-11-12 (the boot of 04:36:49; both containers healthy by 04:37:17)): a subvolume made on the host whose name holds line breaks and two forged list lines (one naming photos, one naming the next volume) showed no phantom volume, and the next volume made through the API was listed once with its path and deleted; GET /health/disks and /storage/disks list sda; scenario.sh volumes and files OK. Steps 1, 3, 4, 6 and 8 are races or failures that cannot be made on the device safely: they rest on the tests. Open on the device: step 7 with a real bind mount.

features.notes: Built (ADR-0275): the rendered [global] turns NetBIOS off (disable netbios = yes, smb ports = 445) and keeps smbd's Bonjour registration on (multicast dns register = yes). install.sh: start_samba enables and restarts smbd and turns nmbd off (systemctl disable --now nmbd); configure_discovery writes /etc/avahi/avahi-daemon.unos.conf (Debian's avahi-daemon settings with use-ipv6=no and publish-aaaa-on-ipv4=no), the drop-in avahi-daemon.service.d/unos.conf (avahi-daemon -s -f that file) and the drop-in wsdd2.service.d/unos.conf (wsdd2 -4), reloads systemd, installs avahi-daemon with --no-install-recommends (no libnss-mdns, which would change the host's name resolution) and enables and restarts it, then wsdd2 the same way when apt-cache show finds the package. Both services answer over IPv4 only: a Mac would otherwise connect from a global IPv6 address, which hosts allow refuses, and wsdd2's TCP ports would listen on tunnels (ADR-0227). wsdd2 is a reserved account name: wsdd2.service runs as the dynamic user wsdd2, which a static account of that name would replace. uninstall.sh enables nmbd again when it restores smb.conf.original and keeps avahi-daemon, wsdd2 and UNOS's files of both, none of them in /etc/unos. docs/INSTALL.md (Step 5, Network Discovery) and docs/USER_GUIDE.md (Finding the NAS) describe it. features.description: A restore never gives two SMB accounts one uid, nor a uid that a user deleted before the backup had
steps: An archive whose smb_accounts holds two rows with one uid is refused
A uid handed out before the backup is never handed out again after the restore
features.notes: Step 1 built 2026-11-11 (ADR-0349): service.check_smb_tables (supervisor/src/shares/service.py), which a restore runs on the extracted database before the account snapshot and the SMB preparation, refuses an smb_accounts table that gives one non-NULL uid to two or more rows, with 400 "unos.db in the backup gives the uid <uid> to <n> SMB accounts", and nothing changes: no copy of the live database, no swap. UNOS's own table keeps uid UNIQUE, so only a crafted or edited backup holds such rows. test_backup_restore.py TestRestoredSchema test_two_accounts_with_one_uid_are_refused (uids 70001 and 70001: 400, the live database, smb.conf and the copies untouched, neither the snapshot nor the account rules run; 70001 and 70002, or no uids: restored) failed before: the restore answered 200. ADR-0349 records the rule, decided by the agent under the owner's delegation, and the option it rejects: clearing the uid of all rows but one, as ADR-0112 does for a uid that a live account holds, since neither restored row has the better claim. Step 2 built 2026-11-12 (ADR-0353, decided by the agent under the owner's delegation): the new table smb_uids (models.SmbUid) records every uid handed out on this NAS with the linux name it went to, and no row is ever deleted. An activation that allocates writes its row in the commit of the row's uid, before useradd, and allocates above every recorded uid whatever next_uid says (accounts._allocate_uid); the reconcile records each stale marked host account before step 6 removes it (step 5', so the first start of a new installation records the accounts that uninstall.sh kept); a restore reads the live table (snapshot_for_restore) and, in prepare_restored_accounts, a restored row whose uid no live account holds keeps it only when the record has no row for it or names the same linux name, else uid NULL, 'needed' and "SMB must be turned on again for X"; the backup's smb_uids is dropped whatever its layout and made anew with the live rows, the live accounts' uids and the restored rows' uids, and next_uid's floor lies above every recorded uid. A backup made before a deletion still brings the user back with the uid. Tests that failed before: test_restore_accounts.py TestWholePath test_the_uid_of_a_deleted_user[bob] (dave activated with 70000 and deleted; an archive giving 70000 to bob: "assert [] == ['SMB must be turned on again for bob']", bob kept 70000) and test_a_reinstall_records_the_kept_accounts ("assert 70000 is None"), TestHandedOutUids (snapshot, the rule for both kinds of database, the record of the restored database for a backup with its own record, none or another layout), test_backup_restore.py TestAccountStep test_the_uid_of_a_deleted_user_goes_to_no_restored_account (the real restore endpoint), test_smb_accounts.py TestCollisions test_an_activation_records_its_uid_before_useradd and test_a_recorded_uid_is_never_handed_out_again, test_smb_reconcile.py TestNextUid test_a_stale_marked_account_is_recorded_before_it_is_removed (all "no such table: smb_uids" before). Review fixes 2026-11-12 (ADR-0353, decided by the agent under the owner's delegation): reconcile step 5' records the stale marked accounts first, then every row with a valid name and uid, so the first start records the rows from before the table and later starts write nothing; begin_user_removal records the deleted row's uid when the table lacks it, in the deletion's transaction; a restore merges the backup's own smb_uids rows with a valid uid and name last, for the uids still missing (they can only reserve uids, and the old installation's backup after a reinstall brings back its deleted users' uids). Tests that failed before: test_smb_reconcile.py TestNextUid test_the_rows_are_recorded_once ("assert {} == {70000: 'alice', 70001: 'bob'}"), test_smb_accounts.py TestCollisions test_a_deletion_records_the_uid_the_record_lacks[missing], test_restore_accounts.py TestWholePath test_the_uid_of_a_user_activated_before_the_record (both cases: "assert () == ((70000, 'dave'),)"), TestHandedOutUids test_the_backups_own_record_joins_last, test_backup_restore.py TestAccountStep test_the_uid_of_a_deleted_user_goes_to_no_restored_account. Limits (ADR-0353): only uids whose user was deleted before the table existed (the dev device) are unknown; an uninstall deletes the record with the database until the old installation's backup is restored. Not checked on the device. Device check 2026-11-12 (main 641f2a5, before and after the reboot from the API at 04:35:30 UTC on 2026-11-12 (the boot of 04:36:49; both containers healthy by 04:37:17)): the database has the table smb_uids with its range check; the device has no marked SMB account now, so the backfill had nothing to record; scenario.sh smb, shares and restore OK (the restore check's activations, restores and deletions with the record). The crafted cases (one uid on two rows, a deleted user's uid in a foreign backup) rest on the tests.

features.description: Every copy of foreign share sections and every import backup is kept, not only the latest

features.description: Samba's own writes to the system disk are reduced: daemon logs in RAM, and no passdb write for a retry of a replaced password or a sign-in of a locked account
steps: On a host whose /var/log is on the system disk, smbd and nmbd log to /run/samba with a small size cap

A failed SMB sign-in of an existing account writes nothing to passdb.tdb while the account is locked or when it retries one of the account's two previous passwords, and any other one writes the account's count of failures, of which the fifth locks it; such a retry writes once when it sets a count older than 5 minutes back to 0 (scripts/dev/sd.sh measure)
features.notes: Built (ADR-0277, ADR-0278). Step 1: the rendered [global] has `log file = /run/samba/log.samba` and `max log size = 100` on every host, since RAM cannot be told from the system disk reliably (zram shows as a block device with ext4) and where /var/log is in RAM the file was in RAM already; one file for smbd, nmbd and the smbd of each client, without %m, so that clients add no files to /run. deploy/install.sh writes the same file. Tests: test_smbconf.py (TestGlobal), test_deploy_scripts.py; test_smbconf_testparm.py needs the device's testparm. Step 2: the account reconcile reads `pdbedit -P "password history"` at every start and sets it to 3 only when it differs, so that a wrong password that is one of an account's two previous passwords skips Samba's passdb write (test_smb_reconcile.py TestPasswordHistory and TestConsistent, against samba_fake.py). A password enters the history only when it is set while the policy is 3 (ADR-0278): an account whose password was set before, as every SMB account on the dev device, has an empty history, so its first change after the deploy does not spare retries of the password it replaced, and only its second change does. ADR-0159 and ADR-0278 took every other wrong password to write passdb.tdb once; measured on the device on 2026-11-09, none does while Samba's lockout policy is 0 (ADR-0310), so step 2 holds as written; limiting repeated failures is shares.smb-login-protection (ADR-0280). Unthrottled SMB sign-ins are an accepted risk (ADR-0280). Device check (ADR-0018), with the SD MiB of each step (ADR-0214): test_smbconf_testparm.py passes against the device's testparm (scripts/dev/bin first on PATH); after the deploy, the reconcile's audit entry says "Set Samba's password history to 3 (it was 0)" once and `pdbedit -P "password history"` prints 3, and the next start reads it without setting it; after the apply's reload, /run/samba/log.samba exists and /var/log/samba/log.smbd and log.nmbd do not grow while clients connect, fail to sign in and Samba reloads; with an SMB account activated after the deploy, or one whose password was changed once after the deploy, change its password through UNOS, then scripts/dev/sd.sh measure around a sign-in with the password just replaced shows about 0 MiB and passdb.tdb's mtime unchanged, and a sign-in with a wrong password that the account never had leaves it as well while no lockout counts failures (ADR-0310); the same after a reboot. Reviewed in a fresh context (ADR-0017): ADR-0278 and the device check above now say that a password enters the history only when it is set while the policy is 3, and ADR-0281 lists the whole [global] with the lines of step 1, superseding ADR-0087. Device check 2026-11-08: smb.conf has log file = /run/samba/log.samba, max log size = 100, log level = 1 auth_audit:2 and logging = syslog@2, and testparm accepts it. Device evidence of 2026-11-09: the smb area of scripts/dev/scenario.sh all, with the runtime files of main 12483dd, at 07:43 UTC and, after the reboot of 12:22 UTC, at 13:58 UTC passed its steps 3 (Samba runs UNOS's smb.conf with a password history of 3), 19 (the replaced password refused, passdb.tdb's time of change as before) and 23 (log file = /run/samba/log.samba, max log size = 100, and /var/log/samba's logs did not grow); its step 21 (a password the account never had, refused; 0.000 MiB at 13:58 UTC) did not look at passdb.tdb then. Measured at 14:24 UTC, after that reboot only (ADR-0310): with bad lockout attempt 0 and password history 3, four sign-ins with passwords a temporary account never had and one with its replaced password each left passdb.tdb's modification time as it was, at 0.000 to 0.016 MiB each; the account was deleted again (1.496 MiB for the whole measurement). GET /audit/logs with the search "password history" answered one entry, "SMB startup reconcile: Set Samba's password history to 3 (it was 0)" of 2026-11-08 04:02 UTC: every start since read the policy without setting it. Since 2026-11-09 the smb check's step with a wrong password compares passdb.tdb's modification time, and its step 3 expects bad lockout attempt 0 (a fresh-context review had found that the step compared nothing). That check passed on 2026-11-09 with the runtime files of main 31ac73b, in scripts/dev/scenario.sh all from 18:25:55 UTC and, after the reboot of 18:41 UTC, from 18:43:12 UTC: its step 3 read no lockout and a password history of 3, and its steps 19 (the replaced password) and 21 (a password the account never had) each left passdb.tdb's time of change as it was, at 0.016 and 0.000 MiB both times. Not checked on the device, and no longer asked for: setting a previous password again through UNOS, which smbpasswd as root does without the history's check (ADR-0278); neither the entry's steps nor the smb check, reviewed on 2026-11-09, name it. Description and step 2 reworded on 2026-11-10 by ADR-0334 (shares.smb-login-protection), which supersedes ADR-0310: Samba's lockout now counts each failed sign-in but a retry of one of the two previous passwords, which writes the account's passdb entry, and a locked account writes nothing until its lock ends. passes is false until the smb scenario check, whose step with a wrong password now expects passdb.tdb to change and whose lockout step expects the refused sign-in of the locked account to leave it as it was, passes with the lockout before and after a reboot (ADR-0018). Device check of the reworded step 2, 2026-11-10 with main bcc4eff, before and after the reboot of 22:01 UTC: the smb scenario check's step 19 (a replaced password leaves passdb.tdb as it was), step 21 (a wrong password changes it, as Samba counts it) and step 22 (a locked account's sign-in leaves it as it was) passed both times.

The tests of the removed paths are removed with them
features.notes: Done in the code 2026-11-10 (ADR-0320, which supersedes ADR-0157). Step 3: no test served a removed path. Open: test_share_repair.py on Linux (scripts/dev/linux-tests.sh), which needs the supervisor's root filesystem in the device's /dev/shm, gone since the reboot of 2026-11-09; making it again (docker create and export) is an owner action. Not host-level: the audit log is the supervisor's file.

features.description: Repeated failed SMB sign-ins are slowed down or locked out, and SMB-bound passwords on a list of common passwords are refused
steps: After repeated failed SMB sign-ins, further attempts from that client or for that account are refused for a while (a rate limit or a lockout)
A password on a list of common passwords is refused with the reason when SMB is turned on with it, and when a user with SMB changes to it
features.notes: Step 2 built (ADR-0279): constants.smb_password_problem refuses a password whose casefolded form is a line of supervisor/src/shares/common_passwords.txt (about 1450 passwords compiled for UNOS, each of at least 8 characters) with "SMB passwords must not be common passwords: this one is on the list of passwords that attackers try first", after the rules of length, size and control characters, wherever SMB-bound passwords are checked. UNOS checks only the passwords that it gives to Samba: Samba's own password change (SAMR) took a common password without UNOS until shares.password-changes-only-through-unos made Samba refuse every such change (ADR-0342), so step 2 holds for every change; and an account that got its password before the list keeps it until its next change. The password that goes back to Samba when the user's own password change fails after smbpasswd ran (ADR-0124) is checked without the list, so that such an account keeps SMB (test_smb_accounts.py TestCommitFailureAfterSmbpasswd and TestSmbpasswdTimeout, test_smb_models.py). Tests: test_smb_models.py (the rule in any case, the order of the rules, the format of the list), test_smb_accounts.py TestCommonPasswords (creating a user with SMB creates nothing; an administrator's and the user's own activation; the password change of an active account by the user and by an administrator; users without SMB keep any password; the text of the E2E fake), users.spec.ts 'creating a user with SMB and a common password is refused with the reason, and creates nobody' (stand-in, the real server) and 'a common password is refused for SMB, and the dialog shows why' (route fakes), account-smb.spec.ts 'turning SMB on with it is refused with the reason and how to go on' (stand-in, the real server) and 'with SMB on, a common password is refused with the reason and nothing changes' (route fakes: the stand-in has no Samba, so no account is active there). Step 2 changes nothing on the host. Reviewed in a fresh context (ADR-0017): a failed change away from a common password that an account got before the list now puts it back instead of turning SMB off, and ADR-0279 names the two exceptions above. Step 1 built (ADR-0334, which supersedes ADR-0280 and ADR-0310; the owner delegated the choice): the startup reconcile keeps Samba's account policies "lockout duration" 5 (minutes), "reset count minutes" 5 and "bad lockout attempt" 5 beside "password history" 3 (accounts.ACCOUNT_POLICIES, ensure_account_policy): pdbedit -P reads each at every start and pdbedit -P -C sets one only when it differs, the threshold after the two times; a policy that cannot be read or set is a problem of the reconcile, and the others go on. Samba then counts each failed sign-in of an account but a retry of one of its two previous passwords (ADR-0278), locks the account at the fifth, and for 5 minutes refuses every sign-in of it, the right password too, with NT_STATUS_ACCOUNT_LOCKED_OUT, writing nothing to passdb.tdb meanwhile; each counted failure writes the account's passdb entry, which changes step 2 of shares.samba-runtime-writes (ADR-0334). Tests: test_smb_reconcile.py TestLockout and TestPasswordHistory against samba_fake.py, which knows the policies with Samba's defaults; test_restore_accounts.py. Device check (ADR-0018), not run yet: the smb scenario check (scripts/dev/scenario.sh smb) before and after a reboot of the deployed tree, with the SD MiB of each step (ADR-0214): its step 3 reads the four policies, its step with a wrong password expects passdb.tdb to change, and its last step that signs in expects 5 wrong passwords in a row to lock the check's account, so that the right password is then refused with NT_STATUS_ACCOUNT_LOCKED_OUT and passdb.tdb stays as it was; the check deletes the account while it is locked (test_dev_scenarios.py). Not in the check, which does not wait for them: the end of the lock after 5 minutes and a count that starts again after 5 minutes without a failure. Accepted with ADR-0334: anyone on the LAN who knows a username can keep its SMB account locked. The threshold is set only when both times are UNOS's: when one cannot be read or set, the lockout stays as it was and the reconcile says why (test_smb_reconcile.py TestLockout). Turning a user's SMB off and on again ends a lock. Device check 2026-11-10 with main bcc4eff: scripts/dev/scenario.sh smb passed its 28 steps at 21:59 UTC (3.895 MiB) and again after the reboot of 22:01 UTC (3.418 MiB): step 3 read the four policies (history 3, lockout duration 5, reset count minutes 5, bad lockout attempt 5), step 21 a wrong password that changed passdb.tdb (0.305 MiB), step 22 five wrong passwords that locked the account so that the right one was refused with NT_STATUS_ACCOUNT_LOCKED_OUT, leaving passdb.tdb as it was (0.133 MiB); pdbedit -P read the same policies after the reboot.

features.description: Failed SMB sign-ins are logged with the client and the account, so that a client that keeps failing can be found
steps: A failed SMB sign-in is logged through Samba's auth_audit class, with the client's address and the account name
An administrator finds these lines in System > Logs and sees which client keeps failing
features.notes: Built (ADR-0277). Step 1: the rendered [global] has `log level = 1 auth_audit:2`, `logging = syslog@2` and `debug timestamp = no`: Samba logs a failed sign-in in its class auth_audit at level 2 and a successful one at 3, the syslog backend takes level 2, and the other classes stay at level 1 (test_smbconf.py TestGlobal); deploy/install.sh writes the same (test_deploy_scripts.py), and ADR-0281 lists the whole [global] with these lines, superseding ADR-0087. Step 2: the source Samba of System > Logs (smbd.service, nmbd.service) lists these lines newest first as notices, and its search finds them by `Auth:` or by a client's address (test_logs_sources.py TestFailedSmbSignIns, against the fake journal; logs.spec.ts 'failed SMB sign-ins: Samba lists them, and a search shows the client that keeps failing', with route fakes: the stand-in has no journal); docs/USER_GUIDE.md (Logs) says how. Device check (ADR-0018), with the SD MiB of each step (ADR-0214): test_smbconf_testparm.py passes against the device's testparm; after the deploy's apply reloaded Samba, a sign-in with a wrong password (for example smbclient on the device against 127.0.0.1 as the account test) adds one journal entry of smbd.service with priority notice that starts with `Auth:` and holds `status [NT_STATUS_WRONG_PASSWORD]`, the account and `remote host [ipv4:127.0.0.1:`; a successful sign-in adds none; GET /api/v1/logs/entries?source=samba&search=Auth: lists the entry and System > Logs shows it; Samba's other messages come without their header line; the same after a reboot. Device check 2026-11-08: a failed SMB sign-in (smbclient with an account that does not exist) was logged by auth_audit with the account, the status and the client's address, and GET /api/v1/logs/entries?source=samba&search=<account> found it. `test_smbconf_testparm.py` against the device's testparm (Samba 4.22.6), 2026-11-08: its logging test expected a `log level` line and `debug timestamp = no`; the dump of `testparm -s` shows no `log level` line, not even for a debug class that Samba lacks, and names `debug timestamp` `timestamp logs`, so of `log level` testparm checks only the parameter's name, never its classes or levels. The test now asserts `timestamp logs = no` beside the log file, its size limit and the syslog level, and all 11 tests pass there (0 MiB); the level of auth_audit rests on test_smbconf.py. Re-check after the reboot of 2026-11-08 (ADR-0018, main 78769b4, the boot of 22:59:48 UTC), from the journal of the smb scenario check's run at 23:03 UTC: its account's two wrong passwords each added one entry of smbd.service with priority notice that starts with `Auth:` and holds `status [NT_STATUS_WRONG_PASSWORD]`, the account and `remote host [ipv4:127.0.0.1:`; its successful sign-ins added none, so auth_audit logs at level 2, not 3; no smbd message of that run has a header line; and GET /api/v1/logs/entries?source=samba&search=<account> lists both entries.

features.description: Repair permissions runs as a background job, so a large share is repaired in one run that the page follows live
steps: Start Repair permissions on a large share: the request answers at once, and the job runs until the share is done, without the 240 s limit of a request
Shares shows the job's progress and its end over the WebSocket, without polling
One repair runs at a time: a second start while one runs is refused
features.notes: Built 2026-11-12 (ADR-0363, which supersedes ADR-0155 and ADR-0006): POST .../repair-permissions answers 202 at once with the job running and walks in a daemon thread of its own until the share is done, stopped (DELETE on the same path, 202; 409 when no repair of that share runs) or 24 hours have passed (repair.TIME_LIMIT_SECONDS; no entry limit); a second start of any share while one runs answers 409 "A permissions repair is already running". The walk reports its counts about once a second, and /ws/v1/events sends administrators {"type": "repair"} with the running job and then its end, which GET then answers as the share's last run; the Repair dialog shows the counts and Stop repair, the share's card says Repairing permissions, and the page reads the shares again at the end, without polling. Backend tests: test_share_repair_job.py, test_ws_auth.py (TestTheRepairOnTheEventsSocket); the walk's stop and progress and the endpoints on real folders are Linux-only tests of test_share_repair.py, not run on macOS. E2E: webui/tests/shares.spec.ts on the stand-in. Host-level (it changes files on the pools): done only after the device check and a reboot check (ADR-0018). Open on the dev device: scripts/dev/scenario.sh shares, whose Repair step now expects the 202 answer running and waits until GET names the run's end, with each step's SD MiB; a second start and the stop cannot be shown there, since the check's share is repaired in moments; a repair of a large share, followed on the Shares page and stopped there, is a check by hand.

features.description: The parser of /etc/exports reads every line form that exportfs accepts and leaves the lines UNOS did not write as they are
steps: Tests give the parser of supervisor/src/shares/exports.py every line form of exports(5): comments, continuation lines, quoted and escaped paths, several clients on one line, default and per-client options
Each line is read as exportfs reads it, or reported as unreadable and left in the file unchanged
Adding or removing an export changes only the lines that UNOS wrote
features.notes: Built: exports.py ports the reader of nfs-utils 2.8 (support/nfs/xio.c, getexportent and parseopts of support/nfs/exports.c). test_nfs.py gives it every line form and checks where exportfs stops reading a file; with the fake host it checks that an add or a delete changes only the lines that UNOS wrote, those exactly in its form (a line written by hand into UNOS's file is listed but never deleted), keeps every other byte, and changes nothing while a file has a line that exportfs cannot read (ADR-0292). Not passing: step 2 is checked only against the port's own expectations, and step 3 writes a host file, a host-level change (ADR-0018); the real sh, od and atomic write ran only on macOS. Open, on the device after the owner installed nfs-kernel-server and deployed: GET /shares/nfs compared with `exportfs -v` for hand-written lines of /etc/exports and of /etc/exports.d (continuations, quotes, several clients, '-' options), and a line that exportfs cannot read named with its file and line; an add and a delete keep every other line of /etc/exports.d/unos.exports byte for byte (sha256 of the file without UNOS's line, before and after), the host's dash and GNU od included; then the same after a reboot.

features.description: An administrator installs an app from the catalog onto a chosen mounted pool
steps: On Apps, the catalog lists the apps by category, with search
Install asks for the pool, and only mounted pools are offered
The app's data folders are made inside that pool, with no '..' and no symlinks, and placeholder secrets are refused
The installed list shows the app with the host folders it uses, and warns about data outside mounted pools
features.notes: Device check: 2026-11-07 (transmission reinstalled with its login on the pool data). Re-check after the reboot of 2026-11-08 (ADR-0018, main 78769b4, the boot of 22:59:48 UTC): GET /apps/installed lists transmission with the same host folders on the pool data as before the reboot, its container runs again, and GET /apps/catalog lists 70 apps by category. The stand-in has no Docker: the catalog cards are skipped there.

features.description: The transmission app installs only with a web login, and its RPC refuses requests without it
steps: Installing transmission without USER and PASS is refused
With both, the container gets them, and its web UI and RPC answer 401 without the login
features.notes: Device check: 2026-11-07 (the RPC answered 401 without the login). Re-check after the reboot of 2026-11-08 (ADR-0018, main 78769b4, the boot of 22:59:48 UTC): transmission's RPC answers 401 without the login.

features.description: An administrator starts, stops, restarts and uninstalls installed apps, and a start first checks that the app's data is on a mounted pool
steps: On Apps > Installed, Stop and Start an app: its state follows
An app whose pool is not mounted does not start, and the answer says which pool to mount
Uninstall removes the container and keeps the app's data
features.notes: Built (ADR-0256): start, restart, stop and uninstall act only on containers with the unos.app label (400 for another container, 404 for an unknown one); stop and uninstall run in a worker thread (ADR-0254); uninstall removes the container without its volumes and leaves the data folders. TestStopAndUninstall and TestStartChecks (the 409 names the pool) prove the steps against a fake Docker, and the Installed apps tests of webui/tests/apps.spec.ts the Installed tab with route fakes (the stand-in has no Docker). On the device: Stop and Start of transmission on Apps > Installed change its state; with the pool data unmounted (an owner action), Start is refused with the message that names the pool 'data'; Uninstall of an app installed for the check removes its container and leaves its folders under /mnt/pools/data/apps. features.description: An administrator manages Docker containers and images: lists them, starts, stops and restarts containers, reads their logs live, and pulls and removes images
steps: Containers lists every container with its state, and filters by state
Start, Stop and Restart act on the container
The logs of a container stream live over the WebSocket
Images lists the images; pull adds one, and remove deletes one that no container uses
features.notes: Built (ADR-0255): the Images tab of the Containers page lists, pulls and removes images, never forced. The server refuses an image that a container uses, running or stopped, with 409 naming the containers; otherwise it removes each tag of the image and then the rest, because Docker deletes an image with more than one tag by its ID only when forced (TestImageRemoval, against a fake that refuses as Docker's classic image store does). features.description: An administrator sets memory and CPU limits for an app's container
steps: Set a memory limit and a CPU quota for an app: docker inspect shows them
The app's page shows its use against the limits, and crossing one sends an alert

(ADR-0254, ADR-0256). A read timeout and an error that Docker answers keep their status (TestADockerThatDoesNotAnswer of test_containers.py and test_apps.py; 41 of its first tests failed before). On the stand-in, api.spec.ts finds the 503 and the reason for GET /containers, /containers/images and /apps/installed, which skipped there before, and the "Containers without Docker (stand-in)" specs of containers.spec.ts find the reason alone on the Containers tab (no counts, search, empty list or Create button), on its Images tab and, with the 503, on the Apps page; both skip on the test stack. features.description: The code for apps that older versions installed under /mnt/pools/default is gone
steps: The checks and messages for apps without a pool label, whose data is in /mnt/pools/default, are removed from supervisor/src/apps and supervisor/src/health
The web UI's types and texts for them are removed
tests/test_apps.py passes without the cases of older versions

Step 2: AppStorageWarning shows only the warning of a pool that is not mounted; the texts systemDisk and systemDiskTitle of the apps catalog and the comments of webui/src/lib/api/apps.ts on older versions are gone, and both fakes of apps.spec.ts that showed the warning are apps whose pool is not mounted. Step 3: the tests of an app under /mnt/pools/default and of an override outside the pools base are gone; test_apps.py passes; 2026-11-12: the last test comment on app data of older versions (test_pool_persistence.py, test_only_btrfs_pools_are_monitored) now names a folder under the pools base that is not a pool. Open: host-level (GLOSSARY.md: the host's containers): on the dev device, an app installed on a pool whose pool is not mounted is listed with its folders outside the pools and its start answers the 409 that names the pool, with the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018), as for apps.manage-installed.

features.description: Docker calls of the containers API run off the event loop, so a slow pull or stop does not hold up other requests
steps: While an image is pulled, or a container is stopped, removed or listed, GET /api/v1/health and other requests are still answered
Every Docker call of supervisor/src/containers/router.py runs in a worker thread, as start and restart already do
A test with a Docker call that blocks shows another request answered meanwhile
features.notes: Built (ADR-0254): every route of supervisor/src/containers/router.py, and the stop and uninstall of the Apps API, call Docker in a worker thread, each request within the client's 60 s timeout (a pull has no deadline). TestDockerCallsOffTheEventLoop checks every route of the router; TestRequestsAnsweredWhileDockerBlocks shows, under a real uvicorn, GET /api/v1/health and GET /api/v1/apps/catalog answered while a pull, a stop, a removal or a listing blocks in a fake Docker.
