features.description: An app can be installed to run in the SMB group, so that it can use a share's folder
steps: Install offers to run the app in the SMB group, which sets its PGID to 70000 (unos-smb)
Such an app reads and writes the share folder it was given; an app installed without the option still cannot
features.notes: Built (ADR-0274): the install option run_in_unos_smb, the checkbox "Run in the group unos-smb" of the app's details, exists for the apps of linuxserver.io images with a pool folder outside {pool}/apps (can_run_in_unos_smb) and adds PUID 80000 (SMB_APP_UID, no other app's user), PGID 70000 and UMASK 007 to the container's environment; other images ignore PUID and PGID, and the option is refused for them and for apps with only their own data. PUID and PGID are no longer environment values (400), and the Environment tab shows them read-only. An install refuses a folder that is, lies inside or holds a share's folder without the option; with it, a share's folder is mounted, and a read-only folder may hold shares, but never a folder inside a share, a share's folder for the app's own data or a writable folder that holds a share. A snapshot folder (.snapshots), the trash (.unos-trash) and folders in them are refused for every app. GET /apps/installed says whether an app runs in the group (runs_in_unos_smb, from its container's PGID), and the Installed tab and the details show it. TestRunInUnosSmb, TestShareFolders, TestInstalledApps and TestConstants prove the environment, the refusals and the list against a fake Docker, and the unos-smb tests of webui/tests/apps.spec.ts the form and the installed view with route fakes (the stand-in has no Docker). Not covered: a share made later on the folder of an app outside the group is not refused (ADR-0274). Open, because Docker apps and share folders are host-level (GLOSSARY.md): the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018). On the device: install a linuxserver.io app (for example syncthing) without the option, then uninstall it (its data stays). Install it again with the option and its data folder set to the folder of a share: it starts, its /config belongs to uid 80000 after the start, and docker inspect shows PUID=80000, PGID=70000 and UMASK=007. Inside the container its user (abc, uid 80000) lists and reads the share's files and creates a file and a folder there, which get the group unos-smb with 0660 and 2770, and an SMB user with write access changes that file. Record the owner, group and mode of the share's folder after the app's first start: root or uid 80000 with the group unos-smb and 2770 passes, any other owner (such as uid 1000) or mode fails. The same install without the option is refused with 400 before any image is pulled, and so is one that sets PUID through the API. The Installed tab shows Runs in the group unos-smb for the app. Uninstall the app afterwards; its data stays.

features.description: The App Store shows the app catalog when Docker does not answer
steps: With Docker down, Apps lists the catalog and says that the installed apps cannot be loaded
On the stand-in, which has no Docker, the catalog-cards test of webui/tests/appstore.spec.ts runs instead of being skipped
features.notes: webui/src/routes/apps/+page.svelte loaded the catalog and the installed apps in one Promise.all, so a failure of either hid both. Passed 2026-11-10 (ADR-0327): the page loads them each on its own, with a state each, lists the catalog as soon as it came, and shows a count only from a load that succeeded. Step 1: on the stand-in, whose supervisor answers GET /apps/installed with 503 (ADR-0323), the Apps page lists the catalog, says "The installed apps could not be loaded: Docker is not available: ...", gives only the number of apps available, and its Installed tab has no count and no "No apps installed" (containers.spec.ts, "the Apps page lists the catalog and says that the installed apps cannot be loaded"); with the answer held on a route fake, the catalog is listed meanwhile (appstore.spec.ts, "the catalog does not wait for the installed apps"). Step 2: "should show app cards in catalog" of appstore.spec.ts runs on the stand-in without its skip. Both of the first checks failed before the change. A fresh-context review found both steps met, and: the catalog still waited for Docker's answer under one loading flag; counts of 0 during a refresh; a spec that matched the tab with its count; an unnamed catalog error; and the record. All fixed. Not host-level.

features.description: An administrator creates a configuration backup, encrypted with a passphrase if wanted, and downloads it
steps: In System > Backup & Restore, create a backup: it is listed under a unique name, also when two are made in the same second
With a passphrase the backup is encrypted with AES-256-GCM and named .tar.gz.enc
Download saves the file with the session, and a download with an expired session leads to the sign-in page
A backup that cannot be created, deleted or downloaded is reported on the page

features.description: An administrator uploads a backup file, and malformed or hostile archives are refused before they are stored
steps: Upload a .tar.gz backup: it is checked in one streaming pass and then listed
Upload an encrypted .tar.gz.enc backup: it is stored as uploaded_<date>_<time>.tar.gz.enc and checked when it is restored
A plain backup named .tar.gz.enc, a corrupt archive and a file over 256 MiB are refused and leave nothing behind

features.description: An administrator restores a backup, an encrypted one with its passphrase, and the configuration comes back
steps: Restore a backup made in the web UI: users, two-factor settings, API tokens and shares come back
An encrypted backup restores with its passphrase and is refused without it
A restore that does not fit into the RAM-backed /tmp answers 507 and changes nothing
A second restore while one runs is refused
features.notes: The SMB side of a restore is shares.restore-keeps-smb-with-proof. A restore renders smb.conf from the restored database and reconciles the SMB accounts (supervisor/src/backup/router.py), a host-level change (GLOSSARY.md): Device check of 2026-11-11 (PROGRESS.md): a configuration backup put into the backup list from an off-device copy, and an encrypted backup with its passphrase, each restored with "success" (database and smb_config), with the users, SMB shares, API tokens, smb.conf and Samba's passdb users the same before and after; the refusals without the passphrase and with a wrong one are steps of scripts/dev/scenario.sh backups, which passed before and after the two reboots that followed. Steps 3 and 4 (507 for a restore that does not fit, a second restore refused) are shown by the tests only.

features.description: A scheduled backup task makes backups and keeps only the newest N scheduled ones
steps: Add a backup task with retention 3 in System > Scheduler
Each run stores auto_backup_<date>_<time>.tar.gz.enc, complete before it is listed, and two runs at once both succeed
The fourth run deletes the oldest scheduled backup and never a manual one
features.notes: webui/tests/scheduler.spec.ts makes a backup task with Keep Count 3 in the form on the stand-in and runs it four times (Run now): each run stores one auto_backup_*.tar.gz.enc, the fourth deletes the oldest, and the Backup & Restore tab lists the three newest and the manual backup. The backend tests check that a backup is listed only once complete and that two runs at once both succeed. Not host-level: the backups stay in the supervisor's /data. Device check: 2026-11-06 (two scheduled backups at once), before scheduled backups were encrypted (ADR-0325).

features.description: Backups of the configuration and of the pools' data are copied off the device and restored from there
steps: On System > Backup & Restore, Save and test of a copy target, a folder on a disk mounted below /mnt or an S3-compatible store with its keys, with the password typed twice (at least 12 characters), opens the copy repository with restic or makes it when none is there; a folder on the system disk, a wrong password and a store out of reach are refused with the reason, and nothing is saved

The repository password and the S3 secret key are kept only in /data/offsite_secrets.json, mode 0600: in no answer of the API, settings or status file, log line, configuration backup or argument of restic

A task of the type offsite_copy, or Run now, copies the configuration archive and the chosen pool folders without their snapshots and trash, removes the snapshots beyond the retention, checks the repository with a share of its data and tests the restore of the configuration; a step that fails fails the run with restic's message and is alerted as a task problem, files that vanished while restic read them are a note, files that cannot be read fail the run once every step ran, and a run while another copy runs is skipped as a success

The page shows the last copy with its files, check and restore test, and the snapshots; Restore configuration puts a snapshot's configuration into the backup list, and Restore files restores a snapshot or one of its folders into a new folder of a pool without overwriting anything
features.notes: Built (ADR-0337): restic in a layer of its own of the supervisor image; supervisor/src/offsite/ with the settings in /data/offsite.json, the secrets in /data/offsite_secrets.json (0600) and the last copy and restore in /data/offsite_status.json; the copy's steps unlock, the configuration from standard input, the folders, forget with --prune, check and the restore test, for the Scheduler's task type offsite_copy and Run now; the restores of the configuration into the backup list and of files into a new folder restored-<UTC time> of a pool; the section Off-device copy of System > Backup & Restore. restic is not installed on the workstation: the backend tests and the local stand-in run the fake of supervisor/tests/fake_restic.py, so restic itself runs first on the device. The test stack skips the E2E main flow: its image has no restic, and its pools share the filesystem of its data volume, which the copy refuses as the system disk. The dev device ran e663f14 with the real restic 0.18: scenario.sh offsite OK (12 steps), and a copy, Restore configuration and the regular restore of that backup left the users, shares, tokens, smb.conf and passdb the same. The review in a fresh context (ADR-0017) of e663f14 found 13 points, each fixed with a test that failed on e663f14 (PROGRESS.md, 2026-11-11): the folders held open while restic runs and the Storage page's refusal to unmount or remove a pool in use, --retry-lock 10m and snapshots --no-lock, the rule for exit status 3, Run now of a task as a task of the scheduler, check --with-cache for s3, the whole disks instead of filesystems, --host unos, and smaller ones. On 8fef386 the device check found that Save with an S3 store out of reach held its request and the lock of the module for restic's 10 minutes: Save and a run now connect to an S3 store first (10 s) and refuse one that does not answer, and Save's restic commands end after 120 s. A second review of 8fef386 led to a UTS namespace and host name of its own for each restic (restic tests a lock of its own host name with SIGHUP to its PID), one copy repository per installation, check --no-cache, the refusal of a disk target whose disks cannot be found, md and device-mapper partitions followed to their members, the refusal of Delete Volume while a copy uses it, and Forget removing staged secrets files. A last review with three lenses and two refuters for each finding found eight more, fixed in c926016: SIGTERM before SIGKILL so that a stopped restic removes its lock, python -B for the host-name step, the disk rule when the disks of /mnt or /data cannot be found, and Delete Volume atomic with a copy, with smaller test and doc points. Device checks of 2026-11-11 (PROGRESS.md): scripts/dev/scenario.sh offsite OK on e663f14, 8fef386, f4ecd22 and c926016 (12 steps each); Save and test refused a folder on the system disk, an S3 store out of reach (within a second since 38a6da5) and a wrong password; a copy before the reboot of 12:52 UTC and one after it, with both copies' snapshots listed; scenario.sh all (101 steps) before and after two reboots. Not run on the device: a copy to a real S3 store and to a second disk, for want of a store and a spare disk; the S3 path runs against the fake restic in the tests.

features.description: Off-device copies also go to a second NAS over SFTP or to a restic REST server
steps: On System > Backup & Restore, an SFTP target (host, user, folder, with its host key pinned) or a REST server with its credentials can be saved and tested as the copy target
Copies, their check and restore test, and the restores run to it as to a disk or an S3 store
features.notes: Left out of backup.off-device-copies by ADR-0337: SFTP needs ssh in the supervisor image, key management and the pinning of host keys.

features.description: A restore checks and extracts the archive in one streaming pass instead of decompressing it into /tmp first
steps: The peak use of /tmp during a restore is at most half of what it is today
A restore still refuses every archive it refuses today
features.notes: Done in the code 2026-11-12 (ADR-0364). A restore reads the backup in one pass over its gzip stream, the pass of the upload check (_read_archive in supervisor/src/backup/router.py), encrypted backups after their decryption in memory as before, and writes only unos.db to /tmp, as it comes; the manifest is read into memory, scheduled_tasks.json only noted, and the SMB preparation keeps its rollback journal in memory. Step 1: test_a_restore_holds_at_most_half_as_much_in_tmp_as_before (plain and encrypted) measures the files in TMPDIR after every call that returns in the restore's thread, for a backup with a database of about 4 MiB: it failed on the code before with 8,540,791 bytes (the decompressed archive, the extracted files and the SQLite journal) against at most 4,257,827, half of the decompressed archive plus the files extracted from it, and now holds the database alone. Step 2: every refusal test of test_backup_restore.py passes unchanged, with the same answers (a member whose data would end past MAX_TAR_BYTES is still a corrupt archive for a restore, as for the decompressed archive, ADR-0364), and so do test_backup_upload_check.py and test_backup_files.py; test_a_database_cut_short_or_refused_after_it_leaves_nothing_in_tmp covers the database extracted before a refusal. The 507 test lost its decompression phase, which no longer exists: a /tmp that is too small now fails at unos.db. scripts/dev/scenario.py restore_check needs no change (its restores answer as before). Open: not host-level; on the dev device after a deploy, scripts/dev/scenario.sh restore and backups must still pass, and neither measures the peak of the container's /tmp, which a step of the restore check sampling df /tmp in the supervisor container during its restores could show.

features.description: Backups refuse files that are not backups at upload, and take the host's pool entries of /etc/fstab
steps: A gzip file that is not a backup, uploaded as .tar.gz.enc, is refused at the upload instead of failing at the restore
A backup takes the pool entries of the host's /etc/fstab, or no fstab at all, never the container's file
features.notes: Built 2026-11-11 (ADR-0345, which takes up the two backup cases of ADR-0167). Step 1: an upload named .tar.gz.enc whose bytes are gzip data to their end (header, deflate data, CRC-32 and length, zero padding allowed, or more than MAX_TAR_BYTES decompressed without an error) is refused with 400 "This file is not an encrypted backup: it is an unencrypted gzip file", and nothing is stored (_refuse_plain_archive and _is_gzip of supervisor/src/backup/router.py); a plain backup still gets "This backup is not encrypted: upload it as .tar.gz". test_backup_upload_check.py test_gzip_data_named_as_encrypted_is_refused_at_the_upload (gzip that is no tar, a tar without a manifest, a cut tar, zero padding after the stream, more than the decompression limit) failed before: each was stored and answered 200; test_an_encrypted_backup_whose_salt_starts_like_gzip_is_accepted guards the other side (an encrypted backup whose random salt starts with gzip's header is kept). Step 2, no fstab at all: no backup reads /etc (Create Backup, encrypted backups, the archive of the off-device copy, backup tasks); BackupConfig and the web UI's type lose include_pools and include_network, which only added the container's fstab and netplan files; a restore ignores the fstab and netplan members of a backup that still holds them, unextracted and without the warning "fstab is included in the backup but is not restored automatically." test_backup_files.py test_a_backup_holds_neither_fstab_nor_netplan failed before (the backup by hand held fstab and netplan, read from the container's /etc), test_backup_restore.py test_restore_database_and_shares failed before (the fstab and netplan warnings), and so did the accepted case fstab-and-netplan-of-an-older-backup of test_backup_upload_check.py (400 "fstab in the backup archive is too large"); test_scheduler_validation.py test_a_backup_task_stores_encrypted_backups allows no fstab in a backup task's backup. Reviewed in a fresh context (ADR-0345 supersedes ADR-0166 after it; USER_GUIDE and CHANGELOG say that only gzip data to its end is refused). Device check 2026-11-11 (tree 8ea5a08, before and after the reboot from the API at 23:22:13 UTC on 2026-11-11 (the boot of 23:23:10; both containers healthy by 23:23:59)): scripts/dev/scenario.sh restore named the members of its backup by hand (manifest.json, unos.db) and of its scheduled one (manifest.json, scheduled_tasks.json, unos.db), neither with fstab or netplan, and passed its 20 steps (7.332 and 7.574 MiB); an upload of a gzip of a tar named .tar.gz.enc answered 400 "This file is not an encrypted backup: it is an unencrypted gzip file" and left the backup list and the backups folder as they were (0.082 MiB), also on main 405d318.

features.description: The backup API has no include_ options that select nothing
steps: BackupConfig of POST /api/v1/backup/create and the web UI's type have no include_users, include_apps, include_scheduler or include_notifications, and the manifest of a new backup names none of them
Create Backup, encrypted backups through the API, the off-device copy and backup tasks make the same backups as before: the manifest and the database, and for a task also the scheduled tasks
features.notes: Built 2026-11-12 (ADR-0355). Step 1: BackupConfig of supervisor/src/backup/router.py has only encrypt and passphrase, and the BackupConfig type of webui/src/lib/api/backup.ts only encrypt and passphrase (the Backup tab sends an empty body, as before). _collect_backup_content takes encrypted instead of the config: the manifest of Create Backup, of encrypted backups through the API and of the off-device copy's archive is version, created, hostname and encrypted, without the config that named the options and would now only repeat encrypt. A request that still sends an include_ option is answered as before (pydantic ignores unknown fields; ADR-0207, no compatibility for API clients). Step 2: the members are unchanged (manifest.json and unos.db; for a backup task also scheduled_tasks.json, whose manifest never named the options). Backup tasks never carried the options: ScheduledTask ignores unknown keys (pydantic's default), so a task stored with them, also in a config object, loads and runs, and the next write of the tasks file (the record of its run) leaves them out; no migration. An older backup whose manifest config names the options (also include_pools and include_network) uploads and restores: only a JSON object is required of manifest.json. test_backup_files.py test_backups_have_no_include_options (a request with the four options, an encrypted backup, the off-device archive, a backup task stored with the options and run, an older backup uploaded and restored) failed before with: AssertionError: assert {'encrypt', '... 'passphrase'} == {'encrypt', 'passphrase'}, Extra items in the left set: 'include_notifications', 'include_scheduler', 'include_users', 'include_apps'. No E2E spec: the web UI's change is a type that no code sends. Device check 2026-11-12 (main 641f2a5, before and after the reboot from the API at 04:35:30 UTC on 2026-11-12 (the boot of 04:36:49; both containers healthy by 04:37:17)): a backup made through the API held manifest.json and unos.db, its manifest exactly version, created, hostname and encrypted (false), and it was deleted again; scenario.sh backups and restore OK (the restore of a backup made moments before, and the scheduled task's backup).

features.description: Restores take only backups whose database holds the shares, and the import of shares from an old backup's smb.conf is gone
steps: Restoring a backup whose database has no share tables is refused with a clear message
The path that imports shares from the archive's smb.conf for such backups is removed with its tests
Backups stop carrying a copy of smb.conf, unless an ADR keeps it
features.notes: Done in the code 2026-11-10 (ADR-0319, which supersedes ADR-0040, ADR-0077, ADR-0139, ADR-0142 and ADR-0143). Step 1: a restore checks the four SMB tables of the extracted database and creates none; one that lacks them is refused with 400 and nothing changes (TestNotAuthoritative test_a_backup_without_the_smb_tables_is_refused, which failed before: the tables were created and the shares imported). Step 2: the import of the archive's smb.conf is gone, with the source 'backup' and smb_state.pending_import_conf; a database without the import marker imports the live smb.conf, never with guest access (test_the_smb_conf_of_an_older_backup_is_not_read, test_the_shares_of_the_live_file_are_imported, test_guest_access_is_not_restored), and its tests are gone or read the live file. Step 3: no backup, manual or scheduled, carries smb.conf, and BackupConfig has no include_shares (test_a_backup_holds_no_smb_conf and test_a_backup_task_stores_encrypted_backups, with the host's smb.conf in place, which failed before for scheduled backups; test_a_backup_restores_the_shares_of_its_database); a restore ignores an smb.conf in an archive, and a database of the previous layout, with pending_import_conf, restores (test_a_database_of_the_previous_layout_restores). The web UI's BackupConfig has no include_shares either. Host-level (GLOSSARY.md: the smb.conf that a restore leads to). Device check of 2026-11-11: scripts/dev/scenario.sh restore (ADR-0341), run from the workstation against the device running main 96db310 (deployed at 15:16 UTC), 15:38:59 to 15:39:58 UTC, OK in 20 steps, 7.207 MiB on the SD card in all; a first run at 15:13 UTC, before the step of the database copies, passed its 19 steps (7.504 MiB), and its two copies of the database were removed by hand afterwards (0.070 MiB). A backup by hand made then, unos_backup_20261111_153913.tar.gz, held fstab, manifest.json and unos.db (0.098 MiB), and the backup of Run now of a disabled scheduled backup task, auto_backup_20261111_153914.tar.gz.enc, opened with its passphrase in the supervisor's container, held manifest.json, fstab, scheduled_tasks.json and unos.db (0.398 MiB, the task and that backup deleted again): neither held an smb.conf. A restore of the first, with the check's share and its access for two SMB users in place and nothing changed since, answered "success", database and smb_config, and kept the shares and smb.conf byte for byte (the same sha256), with the users, API tokens, SMB host accounts and Samba's accounts (0.484 MiB). Re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018), 2026-11-11, scripts from main d6e98c0 against the device running main 96db310 (the runtime of d6e98c0 differs only in a docstring of supervisor/src/shares/smbconf.py): scripts/dev/scenario.sh all OK before the reboot (19:19:48 to 19:25:58 UTC, 146 steps passed, 1 skipped) and after it (the reboot asked from the API at 19:25:58, the boot of 19:26:54, check.sh OK at 19:28; 19:28:15 to 19:34:35 UTC, 146 steps passed, 1 skipped): scenario.sh restore OK, 20 steps, 7.215 MiB before and 7.117 MiB after, both backups without smb.conf and the first restore keeping smb.conf byte for byte each time.

features.description: Scheduled backups are encrypted, because they hold the users' two-factor secrets
steps: A backup task encrypts what it stores with AES-256-GCM and a passphrase, as a manual backup with a passphrase is (.tar.gz.enc)
A scheduled backup restores with that passphrase and is refused without it
features.notes: A backup task needs a passphrase, which no answer of the API and no file holds; the device keeps the key derived from it in /data/scheduled_backup_keys.json, mode 0600 (ADR-0325). The stand-in runs a backup task and restores its backup with the passphrase (webui/tests/backup-restore.spec.ts). Not checked on the device: the RAM a run takes there, and that backup tasks made before ADR-0325 fail until a passphrase is set.

features.description: A user browses the pools and downloads files in the file manager
steps: Open Files: it starts in the pools directory, and .. goes up
Open a folder and click a file's name: the file downloads with the session
A download with an expired session leads to the sign-in page
Paths outside the pools are refused, and symlinks are shown but never followed
features.notes: Step 3: files.spec.ts 'a download with an expired session leads to the sign-in page' (added on 2026-11-07, after a review found the step unasserted).

features.description: A user uploads files into the open folder, and a file appears only when it is complete
steps: Upload files into the open folder: they are listed once complete
Each upload goes to the folder that was open when it started
A refused, failed or cancelled upload leaves nothing, and so does a supervisor stopped in the middle
Bad folders, bad names and form part headers over 8 KiB are refused before any data is written
features.notes: The supervisor stopped in the middle of step 3 is proven on Linux only: there the unnamed file (O_TMPFILE) goes with the process, while on macOS its test is an expected failure. Run it with scripts/dev/linux-tests.sh tests/test_upload_streaming.py.

features.description: A user creates folders and copies, moves and deletes items, and nothing is overwritten
steps: New folder creates a folder in the open folder, and a bad name is refused
Select items, choose Copy or Move, open the destination and choose Copy here or Move here
An item whose name exists at the destination is neither copied nor moved
Delete removes the selected items

features.description: A user renames a file or a folder in the file manager
steps: Rename an item in the open folder: the list shows the new name
A name that exists or breaks the name rules is refused
features.notes: Step 1: files.spec.ts 'renames a file and a folder in the open folder', also from the keyboard, by leaving the field, and after a switch to another window as Chromium reports one; test_files_security.py test_rename_a_file_and_a_folder. Step 2: files.spec.ts 'refuses a name that exists or breaks the name rules, and Escape keeps the name'; test_rename_rejects_bad_names, test_rename_existing_target_is_refused, test_rename_never_replaces_a_name_that_appears_after_the_check. Missing: these backend tests on Linux. On Linux, which the dev device runs, the exclusive rename of ADR-0232 is renameat2 with RENAME_NOREPLACE, and no run has reached it: the tests ran renameatx_np on macOS. passes turns true once the owner's run of scripts/dev/linux-tests.sh tests/test_files_security.py -k rename is green. Device check 2026-11-07: scripts/dev/linux-tests.sh tests/test_files_security.py tests/test_upload_streaming.py passed on the dev device's Linux (259 tests, the exclusive rename with renameat2 included), 0.016 MiB on the SD card.

features.description: The file manager never deletes, renames or moves volumes, other subvolumes or mount points
steps: Deleting, renaming or moving a volume answers 409 and changes nothing
Deleting a folder with a subvolume or a bind mount below it answers 409 and deletes nothing
A volume can still be copied
features.notes: Device check: 2026-11-06 (slice 1 deploy). Re-check after the reboot of 2026-11-08 (ADR-0018, main 78769b4, the boot of 22:59:48 UTC): scripts/dev/scenario.sh files passed (Delete, Rename and Move of a volume refused with 409, a folder with a subvolume below it refused, Copy of a volume), and by hand a folder with a bind mount below it: Delete and Delete for good answered 409 ("contains 'sub', a separate subvolume or filesystem") and deleted nothing; the bind mount and both folders were removed afterwards.

features.description: Uploads time out when the client stops sending, and hidden upload files left on filesystems without O_TMPFILE are cleaned up
steps: An upload whose client stops sending is cut off after a read timeout, and its space is freed
Hidden .unos-upload-<hex> files left by a stop, on filesystems without O_TMPFILE, are found and removed with the owner's consent
features.notes: Step 1 done (ADR-0347): request_limits.receive_upload waits at most UPLOAD_IDLE_TIMEOUT (120) seconds for each chunk of the body, for file manager and backup uploads alike; then it answers 408 "The upload timed out: the client sent nothing for 120 seconds" with Connection: close, and the upload's discard frees its file. A client that keeps sending, however slowly, is not cut off. Tests: the stops_sending and keeps_sending tests of test_upload_streaming.py (ASGI and through uvicorn). Device check 2026-11-11 (tree 8ea5a08, before and after a reboot, by hand through Caddy on the device): an upload that sent its part head and 1 MiB of a declared 4 MiB, then nothing, its connection open, had its unnamed file in the folder held until 119 s after the last byte and gone at 120 s, and nothing of it was left (no file, no hidden .unos-upload-* file, no descriptor); a small file uploaded at once after it was stored; each step wrote 0 MiB to the SD card. Caddy passed the 408 only when the client sent 1 KiB more, at 151 s, and then at once (ADR-0347, Consequences). Step 2 done (ADR-0354, which supersedes ADR-0167, whose cases are all decided now): the supervisor looks for hidden .unos-upload-<16 hex> regular files in every folder below the pools directory (also on mounts there; not in .unos-trash or .snapshots; without following symlinks), once UPLOAD_LEFTOVER_AGE (600 s) after each start (first_upload_leftover_check in the lifespan, a warning in the log only when it finds some) and on POST /api/v1/files/upload-leftovers/check; GET /api/v1/files/upload-leftovers lists them with path, size and modified as the check found them, without touching the disks; DELETE /api/v1/files/upload-leftovers removes the given paths for good after checking every one through its folder's descriptor (400 for another name, 409 for a non-file, an upload in progress or a change in the last 10 minutes), looks at each file again right before its unlink (one replaced or written since is left alone), and drops what is gone, refused or left alone from GET's list. The walk goes at most 64 folders down (deeper folders are named among the problems) and remembers only the roots of mounts (_mount_roots), not every folder. Uploads in progress: _FileUpload puts each hidden name into the in-memory _uploads_in_progress before creating the file and takes it out in discard(). The File Browser shows a notice (region "Leftovers of interrupted uploads") with their number and size and Remove…, whose dialog lists them and asks first (Cancel focused). Tests: test_upload_leftovers.py (also a supervisor killed mid-upload into a folder without unnamed files, whose file the next check finds and the removal removes), the routes in test_authz.py, the first check in test_lifespan.py; E2E: "offers to remove the hidden files of interrupted uploads, and asks first" and "after a refusal, the dialog lists the leftovers that are still to remove" of files.spec.ts on the stand-in, and the notice and dialog in mobile-layout.spec.ts. Not yet checked on the dev device: a vfat or exfat disk mounted below a pool, a supervisor restart in the middle of an upload into it, the check 10 minutes after the start, the removal, and the SD MiB of the check (expected 0). A leftover whose folder was replaced by a symbolic link or a file since the check leaves the list, and the others are removed (test_a_leftover_whose_folder_was_replaced_since_the_check_leaves_the_list failed before: 403 or 400). Device check of step 2, 2026-11-12 (main 641f2a5, by hand, before and after the reboot from the API at 04:35:30 UTC on 2026-11-12 (the boot of 04:36:49; both containers healthy by 04:37:17)): in a folder of the pool, a hidden .unos-upload-<16 hex> file of 1 MiB changed 20 minutes before, a fresh one and a plain file; POST .../check and GET listed the old one alone with its size and time; DELETE of the plain file answered 400, of the fresh one 409, of both hidden files 409, and removed nothing; DELETE of the old one removed it alone; 0 MiB on the SD card. A real leftover from a filesystem without O_TMPFILE (a vfat or exfat disk) was not made: no spare disk. The check by itself ran 10 minutes after the supervisor's start on the device (started 04:40:56 UTC, checked 04:50:59), finding nothing and no problem.

features.description: Folders made with New Folder and files uploaded in Files inside a share are writable for the share's SMB users without a Repair
steps: Create a folder and upload a file in a share's folder in Files: they get the group unos-smb with group write (2770 for the folder, 0660 for the file)
An SMB user with write access to the share changes the file and creates entries in the folder at once
Outside share folders the File Manager creates entries as before
features.notes: Built (ADR-0273): New Folder and Upload give the new entry 2770 or 0660 when the folder it is made in is setgid, of the group unos-smb with group rwx and nothing for others (_share_folder in supervisor/src/files/router.py); the group comes from the folder, and elsewhere new entries keep what the umask leaves. A new folder that cannot get 2770 is removed again, or the answer says that it stays private, since Repair permissions skips private folders. Copy and Move keep the modes of the items, also into a share (files.group-writable-copies-and-moves-in-shares). Steps 1 and 3 are asserted by test_files_security.py, test_upload_streaming.py and test_share_api.py (TestFileManagerInAShareFolder) with the runner's gid as the SMB group, and step 3 in the web UI by files.spec.ts ('outside share folders, a new folder and an upload give the group no write access'); the stand-in cannot give a folder gid 70000. The unnamed upload file (O_TMPFILE) is checked on Linux only: scripts/dev/linux-tests.sh tests/test_upload_streaming.py -k share_folder (both share-folder upload tests, each unnamed and hidden). The device check, and again after a reboot (ADR-0018): in the folder of a share that UNOS created (2770 root:unos-smb) and that gives an active SMB user Read & write, create a folder and upload a file in Files: stat -c '%a %U:%G' shows 2770 root:unos-smb and 660 root:unos-smb. That user then, over SMB (smbclient), overwrites the file and puts a file into the new folder, without a Repair. A folder and an upload made in Files in a pool's top folder, which is never a share's folder, show 755 and 644 root:root (a volume that is shared and was repaired is a share folder: there they get 2770 and 660). Device check 2026-11-08: New Folder in /mnt/pools/data/shared made the folder 2770 with the group unos-smb. The rest is the scenario checks' (the feature-pass skill's table): scripts/dev/scenario.sh smb (step 10: New Folder and Upload in a new share's folder give 2770 and 660 root:unos-smb; step 11: over SMB the share's user changes the uploaded file and puts a file into the new folder) and files (steps 3 and 4: 755 and 644 root:root outside share folders) passed with the runtime files of main 12483dd at 07:43 UTC on 2026-11-09 and, after the reboot of 12:22 UTC, at 13:58 UTC (ADR-0018), as with main 78769b4 on 2026-11-08 before and after its reboot (22:33 and 23:03 UTC).

features.description: Items that Copy, or Move from another pool or volume, put into a share in Files are writable for the share's SMB users without a Repair
steps: Copy a file and a folder into a share's folder in Files: the copies get the group unos-smb with group write (folders 2770, files 0660, or 0770 for files their owner may run, as Repair permissions gives them)
Move a file and a folder from another pool or volume into a share's folder: they get the same modes
An SMB user with write access to the share changes the copied and moved items at once
Outside share folders Copy and Move keep the modes of the items, as before
features.notes: Copies keep the modes of their source (_copy_entry in supervisor/src/files/router.py), and so do moves to another pool or volume, which copy: such items need Repair permissions (ADR-0155), while New Folder and Upload give share modes (ADR-0273, files.group-writable-entries-in-shares). A Move within a pool or volume is a rename and keeps the modes as well; whether it should change them is open.

features.description: Items deleted in the file manager can be brought back for a while
steps: Delete items in Files: they go to the trash of their pool or volume, and their folder no longer lists them
On the Trash page, restore deleted items: they are back where they were, and a name that is taken there again is refused
They are gone for good only after a set time, 30 days after their deletion, or when an administrator empties the trash or deletes them from it
features.notes: Built 2026-11-07 (ADR-0259, which filled in the steps for the trash it chose; step 3 keeps the original guarantee: the Delete dialog offers no Delete for good before the server refused the move): Delete in Files moves items into <pool>/.unos-trash or <pool>/<volume>/.unos-trash with one rename, a private folder (mode 0700) per item with the item and its origin; a trash that someone else made first is made the supervisor's with mode 0700 before it is used, one that cannot be made so is refused (409), and only private folders in a trash count as its entries; every item is checked before any is moved (also bind mounts on the way, from the mount table), and one that fails after others went answers with how many went; the Delete dialog offers Delete for good (?permanent=true) only after a 409 or 507 refusal of the move, and after any refusal it holds only the items still in their folder, with the focus on Cancel; GET /files/trash, POST /files/trash/restore (every item checked first, also that its folder is on the filesystem of its pool or volume and below no mount point), DELETE /files/trash and POST /files/trash/empty; trash_expiry_loop in the lifespan, at the start and once a day; the name .unos-trash is hidden, refused and left out of copies, every share section vetoes it and it cannot be shared; on the Trash page each checkbox is labelled with the item's name, folder and deletion time. features.description: An administrator reboots, shuts down or suspends the host, cancels a pending shutdown, and turns Wake-on-LAN on

features.notes: Built (ADR-0233): reboot, shutdown, cancel, suspend and Wake-on-LAN run on the host through src/host.py; GET /api/v1/power/pending reads logind's ScheduledShutdown, and Cancel runs shutdown -c only while something is pending; the Wake-on-LAN choice per interface is kept in /data/wol_config.json and set again at each start of the supervisor; with UNOS_HOST_EXEC=local (the stand-in, the test stack) every power endpoint answers 503 and runs nothing; POST /system/reboot, /system/shutdown and /system/cancel-shutdown are gone. features.description: System > Logs shows the host's journal, kernel messages and log files, with filters and search
steps: Pick a source and a severity: the entries are listed, newest first
Search highlights matches and shows markup in log lines as text
The filters are comboboxes named by their labels
features.notes: Built (ADR-0257, ADR-0258): every source is a part of the host's journal, read with one journalctl command on the host through src/host.py, newest first (--reverse --lines=<limit>), off the event loop: System Journal (all of it), Kernel (--dmesg), Docker (docker.service), Samba (smbd.service, nmbd.service), Authentication (the syslog facilities auth and authpriv) and Cron Jobs (cron.service); UNOS Supervisor and Web Server are no longer sources. journalctl runs under the host's timeout(1) (`timeout --kill-after=5 30`), which ends it on the host after 30 seconds, and at most two reads run at once, on a pool of threads of their own. In every source a severity lists that level and the more severe ones and the time range applies, and the search is journalctl's literal, case-insensitive --grep, so it finds the newest matches of the whole range; a search without a match (status 1 without output) lists no entries. The output is split at \n alone, so an entry with U+2028 stays one entry. The tab shows the entries in the answer's order, says newest first, shows the times in the browser's time zone, sends a new limit with its request, shows only the answer of its newest request, shows an error instead of the list, and Auto and Search wait for an answer that is still coming. Step 1: tests/test_logs_sources.py (TestSources: each source's command and its entries, newest first; TestSeverity: every level in every source; TestTimeRange; TestEntries, with U+2028, the host's timeout and two reads at a time off the default executor; TestErrors, with a journalctl that reads too long ended on the host; TestValues, TestRoles; the old routes' test left with them, system.no-legacy-log-endpoints) and logs.spec.ts 'pick a source and a severity: the entries are listed, newest first', 'the limit and the time range reach the server with the request they change', 'Auto asks again every 5 seconds, but not while an answer is still coming', 'a late answer for the source picked before does not replace the entries of the one picked last' and 'an error of the server is shown instead of the entries of the request before'. Step 2: logs.spec.ts 'search highlighting shows markup in log lines as text', 'a search asks the server: the matches it lists are highlighted, and no match says so' and 'Search waits while an answer is still coming', and TestSearch (with a search that finds nothing) and TestEntries for the server. Step 3: logs.spec.ts 'filters are comboboxes named by their labels'. Not built: the log files of the description. GET /logs/files and /logs/file/{filename} still read the supervisor container's /var/log and have no view; which of the host's files the API may read as root is the owner's decision. Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018), with the SD MiB of each step (ADR-0214): on the dev device, for each of the six sources, GET /api/v1/logs/entries?source=<source>&limit=20 answers 200 with the host's entries, newest first (timestamps descending), the same entries as `journalctl -r -n 20` with the source's matches on the host (a 200 also shows that the host runs journalctl under its timeout(1)); ?source=dmesg&priority=warning lists only the levels emerg to warning; ?since=1 hour ago only the last hour's entries; ?search=<a word of an older entry>&limit=5 finds it, and a word no entry has answers 200 with no entries (journalctl --grep's status 1 on no match); System > Logs lists the same; after a reboot Kernel lists the new boot's messages. Device check 2026-11-08 after the deploy: journal, dmesg, docker, samba, auth and cron each listed their entries newest first. Open: the same after a reboot. After the reboot of 2026-11-08 the journal was listed newest first again.

Send a test: the message arrives, or the error is named

The certificate check of ADR-0045 (STARTTLS, SMTPS on port 465, the self-signed opt-out) came in from commit bbb773b of the branch smtp-verify-tls, which stays unmerged. test_notifications.py delivers to a local mail server (STARTTLS and SMTPS; trusted, self-signed and wrong-host certificates; a relay that takes mail without a login; the Date and Message-ID it receives) and a local webhook receiver, and fakes Telegram's API; its API tests also let the writes of the channels and the history fail as on a full disk, wait as on a busy SD card, and come two at once; notifications.spec.ts drives the tab with route fakes, and one of its tests sends through the stand-in's own supervisor to a mail server that is not there. features.description: Problems reach every enabled notification channel and show as a banner in the web UI
steps: A pool not mounted or degraded, a failed SMART test, scrub errors, low space and a missed task each send one alert to every enabled channel, webhooks included
The web UI shows a health banner until the problem is gone
An alert is sent once per problem, not at every check
features.notes: The RAID monitor reports the problems of the managed pools (not mounted or no disk found, degraded, read-only after an error, 90% and 95% full), the SMART monitor those of the disks (health FAILED, a failed self-test), and a check every 5 minutes those of the scheduled tasks (last run failed, a missed run); each is alerted once through every enabled channel, webhooks included, while it lasts, and again after a restart of the supervisor, since the list is kept in RAM (ADR-0332). Scrub errors reach the devices' error counters, which make the pool degraded. Administrators see the list as a banner above every page until it is empty. Device checks (PROGRESS.md, 2026-11-10 and 2026-11-11): a failed task's alert went once to every enabled channel (a webhook and Telegram) while the problem lasted, again at the first check after a reboot (10:19:51 UTC), and a task whose time fell while a reboot stopped the supervisor was alerted as missed (13:03:29 UTC); the dev device's real pool and disk raised no problem. features.description: Telegram alerts reach their chat from the dev device's network
steps: A Telegram, webhook, Discord or Slack request that connects nowhere from the supervisor's container goes once more, the same request, from the host's network with the host's curl, and arrives
A request that reached its service is never sent again: an HTTP answer of any status, or no answer in time after the request was sent, ends the send
The bot token, a webhook's URL and its headers reach curl only on its standard input: never on its command line, in an error text, the history or the log
An answer counts the same on both paths, and a send that fails both ways names both attempts, or a host without curl, in the test's answer and in the history
Both attempts end within the channel's time, 15 seconds for Telegram and 30 for the others, and within an alert's 60 seconds
A test notification to a Telegram channel arrives from the dev device
features.notes: Built (ADR-0336, which supersedes the proposal ADR-0046; neither IPv6 for the compose network nor e-mail instead): the HTTP channels send each request from the container with a connect timeout of 5 seconds, and only when httpx raises ConnectError or ConnectTimeout (no TCP or TLS connection, so the request was not sent) once more from the host's network through host.run_on_host_async: curl with fixed options on its command line (--disable first, --globoff, --max-time with what is left of the channel's time, --proto =https,http, --config -, the status after the body) and the request as its config on standard input (url, request, header, data-raw, each value quoted with its escapes, UTF-8 as it is). A request with a NUL character or a header that httpx would not send is not sent from the host. The bot token, a webhook's URL with its path and its header values are replaced by *** in what httpx, curl and the services say; Telegram's answer counts as a delivery with HTTP 200 and "ok": true on both paths. curl joined HOST_TOOLS (deploy/install.sh installs it). E-mail is unchanged. Tests first: 42 tests of test_notifications.py's TestFromTheHostsNetwork (against FakeHost's curl of test_pool_persistence.py, which reads the config as curl does, and one through the real curl of the machine to a local receiver) failed on the code before, and so did 4 older tests that the decision changes: Telegram's connect timeout is 5 of its 15 seconds, and a webhook's refused connection is tried from the host as well. Reviewed in a fresh context (ADR-0017): the headers that curl reads differently, a webhook's key named by its path alone, short values garbling errors, curl's time after a slow TLS handshake and a captive portal's page as Telegram's error were fixed with tests that failed first; the host's attempt in asyncio's default thread pool and a loopback URL that names the host stay, with the reasons in PROGRESS.md (2026-11-11). A host-level change: it sends from the host's network. Device check (main 53396c0, 2026-11-11, PROGRESS.md): a test notification to the owner's Telegram channel answered "sent" at 09:12:52 UTC and was recorded as delivered at 09:12:58, after the container's 5 s connect timeout and the host's curl, and the owner confirmed it arrived. After the reboots of 10:19 and 12:52 UTC the first alerts of the start, "Task ... failed" at 10:19:51 and "Task ... missed its run" at 13:03:29, reached Telegram the same way.

features.description: An administrator schedules a custom shell command

Its output and exit status are recorded with the run
Regular users can neither see nor create such tasks
features.notes: The command runs with /bin/sh as root inside the supervisor container. A run records the exit status and the last 16 KiB of standard output and error together; a command is stopped after 24 hours, and every process of its session ends with it, also those that timeout or job control put in process groups of their own (ADR-0267). A run that a stop of the supervisor cuts off is recorded as failed, at an orderly stop or at the next start (ADR-0268). Step 1: the stand-in's E2E test makes a custom task in the form and runs it (Run now); test_the_scheduler_runs_a_custom_task_at_its_time drives the scheduler loop on a fake clock, since the stand-in runs no background loops. Step 3: the scheduler router is administrator-only (test_scheduler_validation.py, test_authz.py), and roles.spec.ts shows that a regular user gets neither the tab nor the API. On the device, the hour of a run follows the host's time zone: the device check of system.scheduler-time-zone.

features.description: Disabling a network interface asks for confirmation and turns the interface back on by itself unless the change is confirmed
steps: Disable an interface in System > Network: a dialog names the interface and warns that the connection to UNOS may drop
Unless the change is confirmed from the page within a set time, the interface comes back on by itself
A confirmed change stays after that time
features.notes: Built (ADR-0244, ADR-0246): Disable asks in a dialog that names the interface and warns that the connection may drop. POST /network/interfaces/{name}/down saves the interface's addresses and routes in /run/unos/network on the host, arms the transient systemd timer unos-network-revert-<if> (60 seconds) and only then disables it; it refuses (the interface stays enabled) when the state cannot be saved or the timer cannot be armed, and (409) for an interface that carries VLANs without loose binding, which the kernel turns off and on with it. The page counts down, the newest countdown first and with the focus on the countdowns, and offers Keep (POST .../down/confirm); a Keep whose host command fails or does not answer in time answers from the marker on the host. Without Keep the timer turns the interface back on with its saved addresses and routes, also when the supervisor restarts. When the page's time runs out it looks again 5 seconds later and reports what it finds: back on, still counting on the host (countdown and Keep again), still off with nothing waiting (a revert that could not turn it on, or a Keep elsewhere: reported, with Enable), gone from the host, or not readable. Wherever UNOS finds the interface on again (Enable, Keep), it discards the saved state, unless the revert is restoring it. The fake-host tests, the tests of the host scripts under sh and dash and the E2E spec pass. Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018), with the SD MiB of each step (ADR-0214): disable a NIC that does not carry the connection and wait: after 60 seconds `ip link` shows it up again, `ip route` and `ip -6 addr` show its default route and IPv6 addresses again, `journalctl -u unos-network-revert-<if>` shows the revert and /run/unos/network/<if> holds no pending file; disable it and press Keep: it is still down after 60 seconds, `systemctl list-timers` lists no unos-network-revert timer, and Enable brings back its routes; disable it, press Keep, turn it on on the host (`ip link set dev <if> up`) and send `POST /network/interfaces/<if>/up`: it answers 200 and /run/unos/network/<if> holds no saved files; disable the NIC that carries the web UI: the page reaches UNOS again within about a minute; after a reboot every interface is up. Whether the dev device's network manager turns a kept disable back on by itself is unknown until then. Device check 2026-11-07 on the VLAN enP4p65s0.99 (the device has one NIC, which carries the connection): disabled through the API it was down on the host with revert_in 59, came back on by itself after 60 seconds, and a disable that was kept stayed down after 70 seconds; no revert timer was left (0.082 MiB on the SD card).

features.notes: First of two phases (ADR-0287). Built: the lookup and the stores of webui/src/lib/i18n/ (one catalog per area with English and Russian halves, plural forms by Intl.PluralRules, the choice kept in this browser as unos-locale, <html lang> after it, Russian by default for a browser set to Russian, dates in the browser's format when it is of the page's language and else day first on a 24-hour clock), the Language card of the Account page, and the texts in both languages of the navigation and the frame (+layout.svelte, the tabs of the System page), the login and setup pages, the Account page (SecurityTab.svelte with RecoveryCodes and SmbAccessCard; the firewall's and the certificates' values through maps from the server's values to keys, a certificate's openssl dates in the page's language) and the shared components of src/lib/components/ui. Step 1: webui/tests/language.spec.ts switches an administrator's Account page to Russian and sees the navigation and the page change at once, stay Russian after a reload and on the login page after signing out, and go back to English; switches a regular user's Account page to Russian, also after a reload; shows the firewall's and the certificates' values in both languages; and checks that a browser set to Russian starts in Russian and that an English page in it writes dates day first. It cannot see a text that the code puts together from data at run time, a single lower-case word in a script, or a .ts module, so the empty list is necessary, not sufficient: passes stays false until the list is empty and a walk through every page in Russian, by a reviewer in a fresh context, finds no English text other than the server's messages. Second phase, apps: the App Store (src/routes/apps/+page.svelte and src/lib/components/apps/) takes its texts from catalog/apps.ts, names each category with the label of its category list (AppCategory.svelte) and writes the sizes of the pools in the number format and the units of the page's language; webui/tests/apps.spec.ts shows the catalog, the details of an app and the installed apps in Russian. The names, descriptions and variables of the apps and their memory recommendations stay in English, as the server's app catalog has them, so the walk of ADR-0287 still finds English there. ADR-0291, proposed to the owner and not yet decided, would count them with the server's messages and keep the category list's labels on the English cards (Smart Home, AI & LLMs and Downloads, where they said Home Automation, Ai and Download); refused, the cards get keys of their own with their former words, and the app catalog needs a translation before this feature passes. Second phase, the dashboard and Files: the dashboard (src/routes/+page.svelte and its widgets, the containers' states through a map) and Files with its trash, with the units of their sizes, rates and times from their own catalogs and the numbers' decimal point kept (ADR-0297); dashboard.spec.ts ('shows the dashboard in Russian', with the stats cards of a fake stats socket, and a regular user's) and files.spec.ts ('shows Files and the trash in Russian', 'Files and the trash count, size and date their items in Russian') show them in Russian, with the counts in their plural forms, the sizes, rates, times and dates that the code puts together at run time, while the server's messages stay English; dashboard.spec.ts 'the stats cards write sizes, rates and the temperature with their units' keeps their English. Left for one change across the areas (ADR-0297): formatBytes and formatBytesPerSecond of src/lib/stores/stats.ts still write English units, which the translated Images tab of the Containers page shows in Russian too; and the App Store writes numbers with a decimal comma (ADR-0291), the dashboard and Files with a decimal point. The check of the texts does not see either, so the walk of ADR-0287 has to. Translated in phase B: System > Notifications and System > Network (NotificationsTab.svelte and NetworkTab.svelte, catalogs notifications and network), off the list; webui/tests/notifications.spec.ts and webui/tests/network.spec.ts check each tab in Russian (its texts, plural forms, the server's values through maps of keys, a channel's events by their names, dates, and the link speeds and the live traffic of the stats stream in the page's units and number format), and the values that ip and ss print in the Network tab's tables stay as they come (ADR-0295); supervisor/tests/test_notifications.py checks that the English half of the notifications catalog names and describes the server's events word for word. formatBytes and formatBytesPerSecond of webui/src/lib/stores/stats.ts still write English units on the pages that use them. Second phase, the System tabs Resource Monitor, System Logs, Disk Health and Power Management and the Audit Log page: they take their texts from the catalogs monitor, logs, health, power and audit, and the server's values through maps (log sources, levels and time ranges; SMART states, attribute states, NVMe fields and the units of a disk's capacity; audit actions, severities and types of resource). features.description: Pages that show changing data get it over the WebSocket, never by polling the API
steps: Container details, System > Logs, Storage and System > Updates update without setInterval polling

features.notes: Built: no page polls the API. Container details stream their log over /ws/v1/logs/{id} (ADR-0255, apps.containers-and-images: containers.spec.ts 'the log of a container streams live over the WebSocket'), and UpdateTab.svelte asks only on Check again (updates.spec.ts). System > Logs' Auto follows the host's journal over /ws/v1/journal (ADR-0366): the socket takes the values of GET /api/v1/logs/entries in its URL, sends the newest entries as that request answers them, then each new entry of the source, level and search from a `journalctl --follow --lines=all` on the host that starts --after-cursor= the newest entry it sent (or --since=@<the second it read at> when it sent none) and that HostStream.stop ends with its process group when the client leaves or its access is revoked (host.stream_on_host); errors send {"type": "error"} and close with 1000. The Storage page follows a running scrub over /ws/v1/events (ADR-0367): storage/scrubs.py keeps each pool whose scrub was seen running (the scrub API's answers, a status read's failure, the Scheduler's start), an administrator's events socket asks for a read of the scrubs that run at most every 2 seconds without waiting for it, and sends {"type": "scrubs"} whenever they change; nothing is read while no administrator is connected, and a read that a request answered meanwhile is dropped. features.description: An administrator imports a btrfs pool that already exists on the host's disks, without formatting them
steps: Attach the disks of an existing btrfs filesystem: the Storage page offers to import it
After the import the pool is mounted by UUID, survives a reboot and keeps its data
features.notes: Built 2026-11-08 (ADR-0283, which superseded ADR-0282 after the fresh-context review). The pool of a name is the btrfs filesystem labelled with it, or of several with one label, the one mounted or managed under it: GET /api/v1/storage/pools lists those, and Mount imports a pool found on the disks (its dialog says the disks are not formatted). Any other btrfs filesystem that is neither the host's system filesystem nor mounted is listed by GET /api/v1/storage/filesystems/importable and under Found on the disks; POST /api/v1/storage/filesystems/{uuid}/import mounts it by UUID at /mnt/pools/<name>, checks that the mount shows the top level, sets the name as its label through the mount, has udev read its devices again and writes the managed fstab entry. Filesystems on boot or virtual devices (the SD card, the eMMC, loop and RAM disks) or on the system disk are neither offered nor listed, and Mount and Import refuse them; an import under a name that SMB shares, NFS exports or containers of an earlier pool still use is refused. A refused or failed import leaves no mountpoint, fstab line or label behind, and Mount, Import and Create undo a mount that shows another subvolume than the top level. Asserted on fakes: step 1 by test_pool_import.py (what is offered: labels, duplicates, boot, virtual and system devices) and storage.spec.ts (Pool import: the offer, the dialog, the refusals, two filesystems with one label, Mount of a found pool); step 2 by test_pool_import.py (the fstab entry by UUID, the mount from it after a reboot, the used bytes kept, no mkfs, the refusals and what an undo leaves), test_pool_persistence.py (TestMountPool) and test_smb_integration.py (an import under the name of a removed pool serves none of its shares). Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018), with the SD MiB of each step (ADR-0214); it needs a spare disk, which the dev device does not have. On it: (1) read only, first: GET /api/v1/storage/pools and GET /api/v1/storage/filesystems/importable list nothing on mmcblk0 (the eMMC) or mmcblk1 (the SD card); nothing is ever imported or mounted there (ADR-0225). (2) A btrfs filesystem without a label (mkfs.btrfs without -L) that holds a few files, not mounted: Storage lists it under Found on the disks with its UUID and size; Import as importtest mounts it at /mnt/pools/importtest by UUID (findmnt), /etc/fstab holds the marker and the UUID entry, btrfs filesystem show and lsblk show the label importtest, and the files are there; after a reboot it is mounted again with its files. (3) An SMB share on importtest, then Remove Pool: the files stay on the disk. Clear the label while it is unmounted (btrfs filesystem label <device> ''): Import as importtest answers 409 and names the share, and nothing changes; after the share is deleted, the import succeeds. (4) Remove Pool, then label the filesystem with a pool name: it is listed as Not mounted, and Mount imports it. (5) Remove Pool, clear the label, mount it by hand, run btrfs subvolume set-default with another subvolume and unmount it: Import as importtest answers 409 with the subvolume message, findmnt shows nothing at /mnt/pools/importtest, that directory does not exist, btrfs filesystem show prints no label, and /etc/fstab is unchanged; labelled with a pool name, Mount answers 409, it stays unmounted and /etc/fstab is unchanged.
